The building of a [canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal "Canal") was an old idea. Numerous and sometimes utopian projects were devised to build a canal between the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") and the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"). Leaders such as [Augustus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus "Augustus"), [Nero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nero "Nero"), [Charlemagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlemagne "Charlemagne"), [François I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_I "François I"), [Charles IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IX_of_France "Charles IX of France") and [Henry IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_IV_of_France "Henry IV of France") had dreamed of it,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-9) as it is a true political and economic issue. King [François I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_I_of_France "Francis I of France") brought [Leonardo da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci "Leonardo da Vinci") to France in 1516 and commissioned a survey of a route from the Garonne at Toulouse to the [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(river) "Aude (river)") at [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-10)

The construction of such a structure would save vessels (of trade but also the [king's galleys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_galley_corps?action=edit&redlink=1 "French galley corps (page does not exist)")) and goods from sailing around the [Iberian Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula "Iberian Peninsula") which could take a month to complete. At that time shipping was fraught with dangers such as [piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy "Piracy") and the [Barbary pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbary_pirates "Barbary pirates").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Ferrand-11)

The most realistic projects were presented to the King in the 16th century. A first draft was presented by [Nicolas Bachelier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Bachelier "Nicolas Bachelier") in 1539 to the [Estates of Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_of_Languedoc "Estates of Languedoc")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-structurae-12) then a second in 1598 by Pierre Reneau[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-13) and finally a third project was proposed by Bernard Aribat de Béziers in 1617.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-14) These projects were abandoned because they did not give enough thought to the water supply for the canal and provided a system of diversion of water from [Pyrénées](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es "Pyrénées") rivers too complex or impossible to implement. In 1650 another engineer also proposed to divert water from the [Ariège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ari%C3%A8ge_(river) "Ariège (river)") to [Cintegabelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cintegabelle "Cintegabelle") to bring a non-navigable canal to Pech-David near [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse"). Again, the question arose of how to carry water to the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") at a greater height than that of Toulouse.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-15)

The projects were not launched for fear of losing too much money and conviction of the human impossibility to dig such a canal. The major problem was how to supply the summit sections with enough water.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Rolt-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-IE-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-JDB-18)

Nevertheless, [Pierre-Paul Riquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre-Paul_Riquet "Pierre-Paul Riquet"), a wealthy collector of [salt tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabelle "Gabelle") in [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc") proposed a more convincing project than his predecessors. When [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV "Louis XIV") received his proposal through the [Archbishop of Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop_of_Toulouse "Archbishop of Toulouse") (Charles-François Anglure of Bourlemont) in 1662 he saw the opportunity to deprive [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") of part of its resources, and the opportunity to mark his reign with an imperishable work.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Ferrand-11)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Lettre_Riquet-Colbert_15-11-1662.jpg/250px-Lettre_Riquet-Colbert_15-11-1662.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lettre_Riquet-Colbert_15-11-1662.jpg)

Photograph of the Letter, Archives of the canal, Toulouse

English translation:

> Monseigneur,
> 
> 
> I wrote you from Perpignan, on the 28th of last month, on the subject of the collection of salt tax in Roussillon and today I am doing the same in this village, but on a subject far removed from that matter there. It is on the design of a canal that could be done in the province of Languedoc for communication between the two seas Océane and Mediterranean, you will be surprised, my lord, that I undertake to tell you about something apparently I do not know and that a collector of salt tax mixes with levelling ...
> 
> 
> But, you will forgive my enterprise when you know that it is on the order of Monseigneur the Archbishop of Toulouse that I write to you. It was some time ago that the lord did me the honour to come to this place because of the fact that I am his neighbour and servant where to find me the means to make this canal, because he had heard that I had done a particular study of it, I told him that I knew him and promised to visit him at Castres on my return from Perpignan, and to guide him around the area to make him see the possibility. I did this and said in the company of the Lord Bishop of Saint-Papoul and several other persons of substance who visited, all of which was found as I had said, the Lord Archbishop was responsible for drawing up a letter and sending it to you, it is included here but in poor order, because, understanding neither Greek nor Latin, and barely able to speak French, it is not possible for me to explain without stuttering, so what I set out to do is by order and for obedience not of my own volition.
> 
> 
> However, my Lord, please take the trouble to read my mail, so that you may truly judge that this canal is feasible, it is truly difficult because of the cost but it can be seen that the good that will come outweighs the consideration of expense. The late King Henry IV, grandfather of our monarch, wished passionately to do this work, the late Cardinal de Joyeuse had started to do some work and Cardinal Richelieu wanted this achievement, in the history of France, the collected works of the said Cardinal de Joyeuse and several other writings warrant the truth; but until today, nobody had thought about how the river can be used to find an easy route for the canal, because it had then been imagined that the use of rivers and machines for raising water were insurmountable obstacles. Also, I believe that these difficulties have always caused distaste which has postponed the execution of the work, but today, my lord, there are easy routes and there are rivers that can be easily diverted from their ancient beds and conducted in this new canal by natural and proper inclination, all difficulties cease, except that of finding the funds to be used for the cost of the work.
> 
> 
> You have for that a thousand means, my Lord, and I present to you again two of my memoires attached to help you to consider more that the ease and assurance of this new navigation will make the [Straits of Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straits_of_Gibraltar "Straits of Gibraltar") cease to be an absolutely necessary passage, that the income of the king of Spain in Cadiz will be reduced and those of our King will rise especially on farms inputs and outputs of goods in this kingdom, in addition the rights received from the said canal will rise to immense sums, and that His Majesty's subjects in general will benefit from a thousand new businesses and will greatly benefit from this navigation, that if I learn that this plan should please you, I will send to you with the number of locks that need to be done and an exact calculation of [toises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toise "Toise") of the said canal, both in length and width.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-19)

### Study of the project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Study of the project")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Plan_canal_Midi.jpg/500px-Plan_canal_Midi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Plan_canal_Midi.jpg)

Plan of the Project

Compared to canals, managing rivers is difficult but only one canal is required between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. Unlike a river, it is easier to manage the flow of a canal to ensure a constant flow of traffic throughout the year.

The Canal du Midi is a [summit-level canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit-level_canal "Summit-level canal") because it must pass over a height between two valleys. The construction of this canal required passage through the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") or the Seuil de Graissens.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-20)

Thirty years passed from the start of planning to the commencement of work: a similar project was also studied by a committee of which Riquet's father was a member.

#### Highlights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Highlights")]

In 1660, Riquet found the solution to the main problem: the water supply to the summit point to feed both sides of the canal. His idea was to get water flowing from the [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire"). His important knowledge of the [hydrography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrography "Hydrography") of the Montagne Noire and Sor allowed him to imagine an ingenious irrigation system.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-21) He was inspired by the French engineer [Adam de Craponne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_de_Craponne "Adam de Craponne") who had implemented the same system for the [Craponne Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_de_Craponne "Canal de Craponne").

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Canal_du_Midi_Schleusenschild.jpg/250px-Canal_du_Midi_Schleusenschild.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Canal_du_Midi_Schleusenschild.jpg)

Sign indicating the [Océan Lock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oc%C3%A9an_Lock "Océan Lock") at the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") at the highest point with 189m altitude

For this, he planned to recover the mountain waters in dams and reservoirs and then forward them to the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") through channels crossing the Seuil de Graissens. The water from the Sor passing near [Revel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revel,_Haute-Garonne "Revel, Haute-Garonne") was the main supply envisaged by Riquet. Other rivers from the Montagne Noire were also part of the system such as the Alzeau, the Laudot, the Rieutort, the Bernassonne, and the [Lampy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lampy_(river)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lampy (river) (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lampy "fr:Lampy")].[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-22) The Montagne Noire is a region with twice the rainfall of the plain of [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais") with 1400 millimetres per year at around 500–600 m (1,600–2,000 ft) above sea level.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-23) To store the river water he planned to create three basins: the Reservoir of Lampy-Vieux, a hexagonal harbour basin at Naurouze, and the [Bassin de Saint-Ferréol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassin_de_Saint-Ferr%C3%A9ol "Bassin de Saint-Ferréol") with a large earth dam across the mouth of the valley of the Laudot stream.

In 1664, during the study of the project, the [Estates of Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_of_Languedoc "Estates of Languedoc") asked Riquet to put into practice his idea experimentally. He then built a test channel diverting water from the Sor to the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze"). It was the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") which he completed in 1665 and used to prove that it is possible to bring water to the highest points of the course of the canal.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-experience_rigole_plaine-24) This was the event that reassured the Committee of Experts that the king had set up on site to inspect the choices and plans prepared by Riquet. From that moment [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV "Louis XIV") knew that the canal was technically feasible.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-25)

#### Inaccuracies by Pierre-Paul Riquet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Inaccuracies by Pierre-Paul Riquet")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/CdM_-_Bassin_de_Naurouze.jpg/250px-CdM_-_Bassin_de_Naurouze.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CdM_-_Bassin_de_Naurouze.jpg)

Plan of the Basin of Naurouze, which was later abandoned because of its high silt level

Riquet studied in depth the supply of water to the canal at the Seuil de Naurouze. His study appeared rigorous and included a pilot phase with the construction of the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") to substantiate his claim. The project still remained unclear in many respects especially the route of the canal. This route was not final and was not precise as it would be today for a highway project or [high-speed railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-speed_railway "High-speed railway"). Only the directions of the route were known and plotted on a map. Changes in the route could be made by the Contractor depending on the difficulties he encountered on the ground.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-26)

On the Atlantic side, he proposed several layouts: one to pass by [Castres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castres "Castres") and [Revel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revel,_Haute-Garonne "Revel, Haute-Garonne") through the Seuil de Graissens and [Agout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agout "Agout"). In fact, this river was already under development for navigation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-27) Another route would pass by the Girou river and avoid [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") as in the preceding route. On the Mediterranean side, the route was not set. He would use the Fresquel until the [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(river) "Aude (river)") but the arrival on the coast was first intended to be at [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") then at [Sète](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A8te "Sète").

In 1663 Riquet conducted field studies to finally fix the path on the Atlantic side by the seuil de Naurouze along the valley of the [Hers-Vif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hers-Vif "Hers-Vif") to [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") downstream of the [Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garonne "Garonne"). The navigable part of the river is downstream of [Bazacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bazacle "Bazacle") which was a ford in the centre of Toulouse, blocking navigation. The canal could not consider not going through the economic heart of the region so therefore the final route was via Castres and the Girou.

#### Study techniques

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Study techniques")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/CdM_-_Ecluse_Ronde_d%27Agde.jpg/250px-CdM_-_Ecluse_Ronde_d%27Agde.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CdM_-_Ecluse_Ronde_d'Agde.jpg)

Plan of the Round Locks at Agde by Pierre-Paul Riquet

Pierre-Paul Riquet had no technical training and learnt on the job. He regularly practised experiments and field observations. His technique remained highly empirical because at that time applied science and hydraulic techniques through laws or concepts had not been mastered.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-28) Even so, Riquet had a scientific approach as he systematically took measurements of [flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrometry "Hydrometry") and made calculations of volumes. In addition, to overcome his technical shortcomings, he was surrounded by many technicians such as Hector Boutheroüe, [François Andreossy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Andreossy "François Andreossy") surveyor and cartographer, and [Pierre Campmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Campmas "Pierre Campmas") an expert in water flows.

He set up experiments to prove that it was possible to bring the water to the [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") from the river Sor in the [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-experience_rigole_plaine-24) At his own expense, of 200,000 livres, he built a test canal, only two feet wide, and on the 9 November 1665 he opened the flow successfully. When the canal was authorized the next year, this test rigole would become the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-29) He also built on his property in [Bonrepos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonrepos "Bonrepos") a model of the canal with [locks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(water_transport) "Lock (water transport)"), [tunnels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel "Tunnel"), and _épanchoirs_ (spillways)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-30) reproducing the slopes and feeding all with water.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-31)

### Political and economic context

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Political and economic context")]

The economic situation of the country was quite difficult at the time. When [Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Baptiste_Colbert "Jean-Baptiste Colbert") became minister he believed that domestic and international trade was not in favour of the [Kingdom of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_France "Kingdom of France"). The [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Republic "Dutch Republic") could take better advantage of trade and economic activity in the country. The prices of [grain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grain "Grain") dropped a lot and wine production fell in 1660. This crisis caused depreciation of land values and small farms were going bankrupt.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-32) In addition, the region of [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc") experienced religious conflict during the [Fronde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fronde "Fronde"). It was difficult to implement a policy in this area and in particular to introduce taxes such as the [salt tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabelle "Gabelle").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-33)

Colbert then saw Pierre-Paul Riquet and his project as a way to pursue a policy of economic expansion in the service of [absolutism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_monarchy "Absolute monarchy") in Languedoc. In fact, Riquet proposed himself to implement the salt tax and to build the Canal du Midi. Thus, the construction of the canal would permit the creation of a direct passage between the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic without passing through the [Strait of Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Gibraltar "Strait of Gibraltar") controlled by the Spaniards, the aim being to destroy the Spanish trade and establish a commercial flow through Languedoc. The Languedoc region had many resources such as [wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheat "Wheat"), [wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine "Wine") from [Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minervois "Minervois"), [woollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woollen "Woollen") cloth, [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk "Silk"), and [salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt "Salt") which producers were struggling to export due to lack of trade.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-34) By passing through the Canal du Midi, Colbert hoped to distribute goods in the different regions of _[le Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Midi "Le Midi")_ to strengthen royal power and open up Toulouse and its region.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-35)

### The edict of Louis XIV and the financing of the project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: The edict of Louis XIV and the financing of the project")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Carte_canal_royal_-_18%3F%3F_-_btv1b53029748t.jpg/250px-Carte_canal_royal_-_18%3F%3F_-_btv1b53029748t.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carte_canal_royal_-_18%3F%3F_-_btv1b53029748t.jpg)

Map of the canal from Toulouse to Sète, 18th century or earlier

Despite a project that seemed precarious, Colbert authorized commencement of work by a royal edict in October 1666[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-36) after the approval of a committee of experts that looked at the route of the canal for several months. The project benefited significantly from the appointment of an engineer for fortifications and hydraulics – [Louis Nicolas de Clerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Nicolas_de_Clerville "Louis Nicolas de Clerville") – who used his influence with Colbert to start the project. The decree specified the authorization of the construction of the canal, its issuing of [invitations to tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_for_bids "Call for bids"), and its awarding to the designer, Pierre-Paul Riquet, and his descendants. It also gave rights of expropriation to Riquet and describes the possibility of creating mills, warehouses and housing for the operation of the canal. The project formed a tax-exempt "fief" whose owner had the rights of [fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing "Fishing") and [hunting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunting "Hunting"). Finally, it describes the operating procedures including the introduction of tolls, traffic organization, and ownership of vessels.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-37) The king decided to cede the ownership and operation of the facility in a particular order to overcome the potential drawbacks of a work so great. This system ensured the continued maintenance and operation of the canal even if the state's finances are at their lowest.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-38)

The work was launched in two phases each called an "enterprise". The first enterprise of connecting Toulouse to [Trèbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tr%C3%A8bes "Trèbes") was estimated at 3.6 million [livres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_livre "French livre").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-39) The finances of the State, however, were not very sound and the [Estates of Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_of_Languedoc "Estates of Languedoc") were not willing to fund such a project for fear that their funds would be used for unexpected expenses.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-40) So, in exchange for the ownership and operation of the canal, Pierre-Paul Riquet proposed to finance part of the works from his own funds. The rest was to be paid by the State in exchange for profits that Riquet earned from the salt tax. The second enterprise of works between Trèbes and the [étang de Thau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tang_de_Thau "Étang de Thau") in December 1668 cost 5.832 million [livres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_livre "French livre") plus a million more livres for the resumption of work on the port of Sète.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-41)

Ultimately, while the initial budget was six million livres, all the work together would cost between 17 and 18 million livres of the time,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-42) 40% was advanced by the King, 40% by the province, and 20% by Riquet himself, who became the owner. His descendants continued to pay two million livres for over 50 years.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-44)

### Construction of the canal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Construction of the canal")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Beziers_Fonseranes.jpg/250px-Beziers_Fonseranes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Beziers_Fonseranes.jpg)

Staircase of locks from Fonserannes to [Béziers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9ziers "Béziers")

At the age of 63, Riquet started his great enterprise, sending his personal engineer, [François Andreossy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Andreossy "François Andreossy"), and a local water expert, Pierre Roux, to the [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire") to work on the water supply. This supply system successfully fed the canal with water where it crossed the continental divide, replacing water that drained toward the two seas. The system was a masterpiece of both [hydraulic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydraulic "Hydraulic") and [structural engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_engineering "Structural engineering"), and served as an early ratification of Riquet's vision. It was also a major part of the massive undertaking.

Work began on the first "enterprise" on 1 January 1667 with the construction of the trough of the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") then continued on 15 April 1667 with the laying of the first stone of the [Lac de Saint-Ferréol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lac_de_Saint-Ferr%C3%A9ol "Lac de Saint-Ferréol").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Ren%C3%A9_Gast_2000,_p._18-45) Originally Riquet wanted to build a dozen reservoirs but the Commissioner General of fortifications, [Louis Nicolas de Clerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Nicolas_de_Clerville "Louis Nicolas de Clerville"), asked him to replace them with a single reservoir. This was a great novelty at the time – no reservoir-lake of this magnitude had ever been built before.

Some of [Clerville's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevalier_de_Clerville "Chevalier de Clerville") men with experience in military engineering came, to build the huge dam for the single reservoir, the [Bassin de St. Ferréol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassin_de_St._Ferr%C3%A9ol "Bassin de St. Ferréol"), on the river Laudot. The Laudot is a tributary of the [Tarn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarn_(river) "Tarn (river)") in the Montagne Noire some 20 km (12 mi) from the summit of the proposed canal at [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze"). This massive dam, 700 metres (2,300 ft) long, 30 metres (98 ft) above the riverbed and 120 metres (390 ft) thick at its base was the largest work of [civil engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_engineering "Civil engineering") in Europe and only the second major dam to be built in Europe, after one in [Alicante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicante "Alicante") in Spain. It was connected to the Canal du Midi by a contoured channel over 25 km (16 mi) long, 3.7 m (12 ft) wide with a base width of 1.5 m (4.9 ft). It was eventually equipped with 14 locks in order to bring building materials for the canal down from the mountains and to create a new port for the mountain town of [Revel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revel,_Haute-Garonne "Revel, Haute-Garonne").

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/TunnelduMalpas.jpg/250px-TunnelduMalpas.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TunnelduMalpas.jpg)

World's first canal tunnel, at Malpas

In November 1667 an official ceremony laid the foundation stone of the Garonne lock in Toulouse in the presence of representatives of the [Parlement of Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parlement_of_Toulouse "Parlement of Toulouse"), the _[Capitouls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitouls "Capitouls")_ (sheriffs), and the [Archbishop of Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop_of_Toulouse "Archbishop of Toulouse"), Charles-François d'Anglure de Bourlemont.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-46) A first filling of water was made between the seuil de Naurouze and Toulouse during the winter of 1671–1672 and the first boat traffic could begin. In 1673 the section from Naurouze to Trèbes was completed marking the end of the first "enterprise".

From 1671 the second enterprise began linking [Trèbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tr%C3%A8bes "Trèbes") to the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea") and to build the port of [Sète](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A8te "Sète") (then called _Cette_, the location was chosen and the port constructed by Clerville). This part of the canal posed problems at the junction between the [étang de Thau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tang_de_Thau "Étang de Thau") and Trèbes because the canal must cross the course of the [Hérault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rault_(river) "Hérault (river)") and the Libron. To work around the problem, Riquet set up a system of valves and chambers for Libron and a round lock with three doors for the [étang de Thau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tang_de_Thau "Étang de Thau") and the [Hérault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rault_(river) "Hérault (river)").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-47) The round lock at [Agde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agde "Agde") could switch between a reach of the Canal du Midi and the Hérault. This part of the canal was also a problem at the level of the seuil of Ensérune and the descent to [Beziers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beziers "Beziers") in the valley of the [Orb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orb_(river) "Orb (river)"). Riquet solved these problems on the one hand by digging the [Malpas Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malpas_Tunnel "Malpas Tunnel") and secondly by building at Fonserannes a row of [eight lock chambers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonserannes_Locks "Fonserannes Locks") to the Orb. The [Malpas Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malpas_Tunnel "Malpas Tunnel") was the first canal passage ever built through a tunnel. The Canal du Midi passes through a 173-metre (568 ft) tunnel through a hill at the [Oppidum d'Ensérune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppidum_d'Ens%C3%A9rune "Oppidum d'Ensérune").

In 1681 work on the canal ended at Béziers. However, in October 1680, Riquet died during construction. He did not see the end of the project. It was the king's engineer, _La Feuille_, who took over.

His sons inherited the canal, but the family's investments were not recovered and debts not fully paid until over 100 years later. The canal was well managed and run as a paternalistic enterprise until the [revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution").

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Pompertuzat_-_Pont_Deyme_%282%29.jpg/250px-Pompertuzat_-_Pont_Deyme_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pompertuzat_-_Pont_Deyme_(2).jpg)

The Canal du Midi and Deyme bridge in [Pompertuzat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompertuzat "Pompertuzat")

The canal was built on a grand scale, with oval shaped locks 30.5 m (100 ft) long, 6 m (20 ft) wide at the gates and 11 m (36 ft) wide in the middle. This design was intended to resist the collapse of the walls that happened early in the project. The oval locks used the strength of the arch against the inward pressure of the surrounding soil that had destabilized the early locks with straight walls.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Rolt-16) Such arches had been used by the Romans for retaining walls in [Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul"), so this technique was not new, but its application to locks was revolutionary and was imitated in early American canals.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-IE-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-JDB-18)

Many of the structures were designed with neoclassical elements to further echo the king's ambitions to make France a New Rome. The Canal du Midi as a grand piece of infrastructural engineering in itself was promoted as worthy of Rome and the political dreams behind it were clarified with plaques in Latin, and walls built with Roman features.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-IE-17)

In May 1681 the channel was thoroughly inspected by order of the king to check the work and the water-tightness of the canal. It was then officially opened to navigation on 15 May 1681. At the inauguration of the canal at Toulouse on 15 May, the King's steward and the president of the [Estates of Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_of_Languedoc "Estates of Languedoc") travelled first on the canal followed by many other boats carrying particularly [wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheat "Wheat"). After the maiden voyage, the canal was drained as the work was not complete; it would not be reopened until December 1682.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-48) The canal was opened to traffic in May 1683 and stopped receiving public works in March 1685.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-49)

#### Work organization and social conditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Work organization and social conditions")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/France_Canal_du_Midi_%C3%A9panchoir_de_Naurouze.jpg/250px-France_Canal_du_Midi_%C3%A9panchoir_de_Naurouze.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:France_Canal_du_Midi_%C3%A9panchoir_de_Naurouze.jpg)

The Naurouze Spillway built by stonemasons

For fifteen years nearly 12,000 workers worked on the construction of the canal. Riquet hired men and women between 20 and 50 years old whom he organized in sections forming workshops led by a controller-general. This [rationalization of work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_management "Scientific management") permitted the optimisation of tasks and allowed several projects to be performed at the same time. All of the work was manual and the digging of the canal was with [shovels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shovel "Shovel") and [pickaxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickaxe "Pickaxe"). The workforce was made up of farmers and local workers whose number varied from one period to another during the year. Pierre-Paul Riquet appealed to the military to compensate for this fluctuation. He also set up monthly payments of workers for their loyalty.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Ren%C3%A9_Gast_2000,_p._18-45) He also offered accommodation for two [deniers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_denier "French denier") per day.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-50)

The women labourers were surprisingly important to the canal's engineering. Many came from former [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") bath colonies in the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), where elements of classical hydraulics had been maintained as a living tradition. They were employed at first to move earth to the dam at Saint Ferréol, but their supervisors, who were struggling to design the channels from the dam to the canal, recognized their expertise. Engineering in this period was mainly focused on fortress construction, and hydraulics was concerned mostly with mining and problems of drainage. Building a navigational canal across the continent was well beyond the formal knowledge of the military engineers expected to supervise it, but the peasant women who were carriers of classical hydraulic methods added to the repertoire of available techniques. They not only perfected the water supply system for the canal but also threaded the waterway through the mountains near Béziers, using few locks, and built the eight-lock staircase at Fonserannes.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-IE-17)

The financial and social conditions of employment of the workers were very favourable and unusual for the time. To retain his workforce, Riquet paid his workers well enough. More importantly, he gave benefits never before seen such as non-working rain days, Sundays and public holidays, and finally paid sick leave. The [employment contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employment_contract "Employment contract") was individual and done by free recruitment. Pay was, at the beginning, 20 [sols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_sol "French sol") (1 [livre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_livre "French livre")) per day, double the agricultural wage. Discontent from farm owners, however, forced Riquet to reduce pay to 15, then 12 sols per day. In 1668 he established the monthly payment of 10 [livres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_livre "French livre").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-51)

#### Trades and work measures implemented

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Trades and work measures implemented")]

Many trades were found on the work sites of the canal in addition to the seasonal workers who were most often farmers. The [masons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_mason "Stone mason") and [stonecutters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonemasonry "Stonemasonry") were responsible for the construction of structures such as [bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge "Bridge"), [locks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(water_transport) "Lock (water transport)"), and [spillways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spillway "Spillway"). The [blacksmiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacksmith "Blacksmith") and levellers were responsible for the maintenance of the tools and equipment. Carters and carriers, the [Farriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farrier "Farrier") and owners of [sawmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawmill "Sawmill") were also requisitioned for the works.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-52)

Workers were organized into sections controlled by captains and sergeants. Finally, Pierre-Paul Riquet was surrounded by aides as well as auditor-generals and inspector-generals of the canal.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-53)

The workers' tools were very limited: picks, hoes and shovels to dig, baskets and stretchers to transport materials. They were provided to workers who must maintain them themselves. [Gunpowder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunpowder "Gunpowder") was used to blast the rocks.

### Inauguration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Inauguration")]

In 1681 the first inspection took place "dry".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-54) The king appointed a commission composed of Henri d'Aguessau, steward of Languedoc, Mr de la Feuille, Father Mourgues a Jesuit professor of [rhetoric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhetoric "Rhetoric") and mathematics at the [University of Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Toulouse "University of Toulouse"), two sons and two in-laws of Pierre-Paul Riquet, as well as Messrs. [Andréossy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Andr%C3%A9ossy "François Andréossy"), Gilade, and Contigny. This commission embarked for Beziers on 2 May 1681 and went up the canal back to Toulouse over six days. The filling with water had been done showing a measure of the progress of checks to Castelnaudary (the section Toulouse-Castelnaudary had water since 1672).

The inauguration itself took place just after the first inspection. The same people re-embarked at Toulouse on 15 May 1681 on a flagship boat followed by dozens of other boats. The [Cardinal de Bonzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piero_de_Bonzi "Piero de Bonzi"), Archbishop of Narbonne and President-born of the [Estates of Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_of_Languedoc "Estates of Languedoc") joined the procession which arrived at Castelnaudary on 17 May. A great religious ceremony took place on 18 May at the Church of Saint-Roch followed by a procession to the canal to bless the work, the convoy, and the people present.

The convoy resumed its progress on 20 May with stops in the evening at Villepinte, on the 21st at Penautier, the 22nd at Puicheric, and the 23rd at Roubia. On 24 May it was the passage through the [Malpas Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malpas_Tunnel "Malpas Tunnel") then crossing the locks of Fonsérannes. The cardinal and the bishops went down to Beziers on the same day.

### Supplementary works

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Supplementary works")]

In 1686, [Vauban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vauban "Vauban") was made responsible for inspecting the channel which he quickly found was in a dilapidated state.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-55) He then ordered Antoine Niquet, the engineer of fortifications for Languedoc, to carry out new work at the [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire") level to drill the Cammazes Tunnel to extend the [Rigole de la montagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_montagne "Rigole de la montagne") and strengthen the [Bassin de Saint-Ferréol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassin_de_Saint-Ferr%C3%A9ol "Bassin de Saint-Ferréol"). In his haste, Riquet had underestimated the number of rivers that in case of a flood would silt up and swell the canal. The barrage of Saint-Ferréol was too small and its supply system was inefficient.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-56)

Vauban also built many masonry structures to isolate the many rivers that flow into the canal and spillways to regulate the water level. He built 49 culverts and aqueducts, including the [Cesse aqueduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesse_Aqueduct "Cesse Aqueduct"), the [Orbiel aqueduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbiel_Aqueduct "Orbiel Aqueduct") and the Pechlaurier culvert. Finally, he reinforced a lot of works and dams originally built by Riquet. This series of works, which lasted until 1694, greatly improved the supply and management of water. Antoine Niquet was responsible for monitoring the canal until 1726.

The Canal du Midi still had shortcomings because it did not pass through [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") nor [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") and did not join the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne "Rhône"). In addition, to reach [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux"), it was necessary to take the [Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garonne "Garonne") which has variable flow rates and violent floods. The _Canal de Jonction_ or 'junction canal', built in 1776, gave access to Narbonne via the [Canal de la Robine de Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_de_la_Robine_de_Narbonne "Canal de la Robine de Narbonne"). The same year the [Canal de Brienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_de_Brienne "Canal de Brienne") allowed the bypass of [Bazacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bazacle "Bazacle") - the ford on the Garonne in Toulouse which blocked the river. The connection between the [étang de Thau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tang_de_Thau "Étang de Thau") and the [Rhone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhone "Rhone") was also completed in 1808.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-57) In 1810 a diversion canal allowed Carcassonne to be connected. Finally, in 1857 the [Canal latéral à la Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_Lat%C3%A9ral_de_la_Garonne "Canal Latéral de la Garonne") was opened between [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") and [Castets-en-Dorthe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castets-en-Dorthe "Castets-en-Dorthe"), completing the link between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea that Riquet had dreamt of.

#### Management

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Management")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Xvolks_canal_du_midi_01.jpg/250px-Xvolks_canal_du_midi_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Xvolks_canal_du_midi_01.jpg)

Canal du Midi: on the left the 'chemin de la flegme', in the centre the round lock at Agde, at the right the Bois de Boulogne

Channel management was ensured primarily by the descendants of Riquet. This was through the elder son Jean-Mathias who took control of the fief until 1714, then Victor-Pierre-François until 1760, then Victor-Maurice, and finally Jean-Gabriel. The Riquet family quickly put up a pyramidal organisation structure with a "Director-General of the Canal" who governs a board of directors responsible for specific geographic areas of the channel. Seven zones were defined in the west and the east: Toulouse, Naurouze, Castelnaudary, Trèbes [Le Somail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Somail "Le Somail"), Beziers, and [Agde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agde "Agde"). Each Director is responsible for maintenance of his zone and is supported by a receiver and a controller. Hundreds of lock-keepers are responsible for the locks. This organization facilitates the control and hiring of employees.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-58)

In Toulouse, a group of three people form a steering committee: the director general of works, the Receiver General who sets the fees, and the Comptroller General in charge of accounting. Canal management ensures the supply of money to pay for various works and staff hired for the canal. In the 1770s a tax report showed an income of 640,000 [livres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_livre "French livre"), half of which went to maintenance and salaries, and half the profits and funds were exceptional works. In 1785 this benefit increased to 950,000 livres which was a very large sum for the time.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-59)

#### Maintenance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Maintenance")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/France_Canal_du_Midi_p%C3%A9niche_VNF.jpg/250px-France_Canal_du_Midi_p%C3%A9niche_VNF.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:France_Canal_du_Midi_p%C3%A9niche_VNF.jpg)

Today canal maintenance is done by barges of [Waterways of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterways_of_France "Waterways of France").

The maintenance of the canal was a real problem for the descendants of Riquet. Despite many precautions, the canal silts up with silt from the water supply. In addition, it fills with the branches and leaves of trees. Every winter, a period of closure allows the cleaning of the canal. It is necessary to re-dig the canal bed every year for two months. These works are expensive and two months is not always sufficient.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-60) Another problem is the invasion of the canal by weeds in the levels and spillways. There is no way to eradicate this scourge. In 1820 dredging was set up to pull up the weeds and the mud layer.

Finally, [rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain "Rain"), [frost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frost "Frost"), and [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought "Drought") forces managers to keep an eye all along the canal to repair leaks and cracks that might open. Today, the channel is subject to the same constraints and managers must perform the same work. They are now mechanized. Approximately 350 employees are made available to the Waterways of France manager by the [Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Ecology,_Sustainable_Development_and_Energy "Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Energy") to maintain the canal.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-61)

## Operational history of the canal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Operational history of the canal")]

Once used to transport goods and people, the Canal du Midi is now mainly used by boaters and other tourists.

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Canal_du_Midi%2C_Vias%2C_H%C3%A9rault_%2806%29.jpg/250px-Canal_du_Midi%2C_Vias%2C_H%C3%A9rault_%2806%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Canal_du_Midi,_Vias,_H%C3%A9rault_(06).jpg)

A boat on the Canal du Midi, Vias, Hérault

Initially, the canal appears to have been mainly used by small sailing barges with easily lowered masts, bow-hauled by gangs of men. By the middle of the 18th century, horse towing had largely taken over and steam tugs came in 1834 to cross the Étang. By 1838 273 vessels were regularly working the canal and passenger and packet boats for mail continued a brisk trade until the coming of the railways in 1857.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-62)

A "malle-poste" postal service was set up on boats along the canal. As for the [Stagecoach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach "Stagecoach") for the mail, the boats were pulled by horses on [towpaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Towpath "Towpath"). This type of transport was considered revolutionary thanks to its regularity, comfort, safety, and speed that were an improvement over the road. In addition, the canal could be travelled throughout the year. The journey takes four days from [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") to [Sète](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A8te "Sète").

This time was reduced to 32 hours in 1855 which corresponds to a speed of 11 kilometres per hour (6.8 mph) thanks to the replacement of horses every 10 kilometres (6.2 mi)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-ReferenceA-63) pulling boats. In addition rather than cross multiple locks travellers were transferred from one vessel to another which saved time and saved water used for the opening of the locks. Finally, the journeys also took place at night to save even more time. In 1684, travel from Toulouse to Agde cost one livre and a half. The rate was set per [league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_(unit) "League (unit)") with the rates displayed on a sign. Thus, a [bourgeois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeois "Bourgeois") paid three [sols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_sol "French sol") per league while a [valet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valet "Valet") or a [sailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sailor "Sailor") paid one and a half sols per league. Payment offices were located along the route. Each office indicated the rate and provided the distances between each office.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-64)

Evolution of the number of passengers[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-65)| Year | Number of passengers |
| --- | --- |
| 1682 | 3,750 (over 6 months) |
| 1740 | 12,500 |
| 1783 | 29,400 |
| 1831 | 71,000 |
| 1854 | 94,000 |
| 1856 | 100,000 |

The Canal relied on wheat and wine traffic in Languedoc which was its main purpose. This commercial traffic had the effect of enriching the descendants of Riquet very quickly. The [wheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheat "Wheat"), [wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine "Wine"), and [alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_(drug) "Alcohol (drug)") could be exported from [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais") to [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse"), [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux"), and [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marseille "Marseille"). The canal had the effect of broadening the sales area of the producers of Languedoc. In the 1730s commerce thrived and greatly improved agricultural businesses. The canal also allowed the import to Languedoc of products from other regions such as [Marseille soap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marseille_soap "Marseille soap"), [rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice "Rice"), [starch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starch "Starch"), [dried fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dried_fish "Dried fish"), and [spices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spices "Spices") and [dyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dye "Dye"). However, it was never the grand international route envisaged by the kings of France as its traffic was limited to local and national trade.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-66)

Freight rates depend on the cargo. Thus in the 17th century, the transportation of wheat cost 12 [deniers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_denier "French denier") per [quintal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quintal "Quintal") and that of oats 6 deniers per quintal.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-67)

### The boats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: The boats")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/P%C3%A9niche_Le_Tourville_%C3%A9cluse_de_l_Aiguille_Canal-du-Midi.JPG/250px-P%C3%A9niche_Le_Tourville_%C3%A9cluse_de_l_Aiguille_Canal-du-Midi.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P%C3%A9niche_Le_Tourville_%C3%A9cluse_de_l_Aiguille_Canal-du-Midi.JPG)

The barge _Le Tourville_ in the lock chamber of Aiguille, a newer boat

At its opening the canal was used by a majority of boats for the transport of goods. These vessels were twenty metres long and were hauled by horses or men.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-bateaux-68) The tonnage of vessels increased over the centuries, from 60 tonnes at the beginning to 120 tonnes at the start of the 19th century. The proper Canal [Barges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barge "Barge") were called "owned barge" or "canal barge" and also plied the route. In 1778 there were about 250 barges.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-69) In 1914, there were 126 "owned boats", 70 rented boats, 300 horses, and 75 mules.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-70) In the year 1930 motor barges had completely replaced animal traction. They relaunched in part the merchant traffic on the canal but commercial and merchant inland water shipping finally disappeared around the late 1980s. The year 1856 was a record year for merchant activity with more than 110 million tonnes-kilometres of cargo and nearly 100,000 passengers carried.

For 250 years, horses have pulled many boats such as fast barges or long commercial boats. A horse can tow up to 120 times its weight when the load is on the water. Animal traction was then a strategic element in the operation of a canal.

The mail-barges or "post vehicles" which transported passengers were boats many metres long with a simple shelter on the deck. These boats evolved to become faster and more luxurious with lounges and were very large since the largest could reach 30 metres (98 ft) long. Services inside these vessels also evolved with first class in private salons and second class in a common room. During the heyday of the canal some boats included first class lounges where dinner was served.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-bateaux-68)

### Rail competition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Rail competition")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Toulouse_gare_matabiau_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg/250px-Toulouse_gare_matabiau_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Toulouse_gare_matabiau_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg)

The Canal du Midi in front of the Matabiau Railway Station (opened in 1866) in Toulouse

Curiously, the canal did not really serve its purpose. The economic and political context hindered the economic development that had been expected. After two hundred years of operation, the canal began to suffer from competition from rail and road. It reached its peak in the middle of the 19th century. In 1858 [Napoleon III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_III "Napoleon III") signed a decree entrusting the canal for a period of 40 years to the [Chemins de fer du Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemins_de_fer_du_Midi "Chemins de fer du Midi") railway company, the owner of the Bordeaux-Narbonne railway line. This act had the effect of amplifying the decline in boat traffic on the canal. The company primarily promoted the railway and placed higher freight rates on commercial traffic in the canal. The Canal du Midi had the highest rates of any of France's waterway. In addition, the railway became smoother and faster than the waterway especially as the Canal du Midi suffered from its limited tonnage.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-71)

**Evolution of Merchandise traffic in the 19th century**[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Marconis_et_Lacaze-72)| Year | 1854 | 1856 | 1859 | 1879 | 1889 | 1896 | 1900 | 1909 |
| --- |
| Millions of [tonnes-kilometres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne-kilometre "Tonne-kilometre") | 67 | 110 | 59 | 54 | 32 | 28 | 66 | 80 |

The period before 1859 corresponded to the canal operating without competition while from 1859 the installation of railways in the south of France began. The effect of rail competition is clearly visible in the table with the halving of freight traffic between 1856 and 1879. The traffic then continued to decline gradually. As for the railway, the [Bordeaux–Sète railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux%E2%80%93S%C3%A8te_railway "Bordeaux–Sète railway") carried almost 200 million tonne-kilometres in 1860.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-73) Management of the canal was taken over by the State in 1898 who made successive investments to maintain its competitiveness. The state removed taxes and tolls which had the effect of reviving traffic on the canal to which reached 80 million tonne-kilometres in 1909.

### The end of merchant traffic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: The end of merchant traffic")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Toulouse_minimes_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg/250px-Toulouse_minimes_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Toulouse_minimes_canal_du_midi_postcard.jpg)

Transport of goods at [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse")

The government tried to revive the renovation of the canal by enacting a legal program to lift the channel to the standards of the [Freycinet gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freycinet_gauge "Freycinet gauge"). The canals of northern France were already at this level and had traffic well above the Canal du Midi. However, the law remained unimplemented due to lack of funds.

Evolution of merchant traffic in the 20th century[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-Marconis_et_Lacaze-72)| Year | 1918 | 1939 | 1970 | 1979 |
| --- |
| Millions of [tonnes-kilometres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne-kilometre "Tonne-kilometre") (tkm) | 19 | 100 | 110 | 40 |

At the end of the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War") traffic was completely disorganized. In 1920 freight traffic recovered rapidly with the arrival of motorised barges. The HPLM company (Le Havre-Paris-Lyon-Marseille) operated 30 boats on the Canal du Midi. The [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") saw a slowdown in traffic due to the shortage of [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil "Oil") but recovery was rapid after the conflict and the traffic reached 110 million km. However, the canal suffered from a size too small for later barges with high tonnage. Rail became more and more competitive and road transport also became a second competitor. The Canal du Midi became the third means of transport.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-74) Freight traffic ceased in the 1970s. In 1980 there were only two barges (the _Bacchus_, a wine carrier and the _Espérance_, a grain carrier) carrying regular traffic between [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") and [Sète](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A8te "Sète"): they definitively ceased their activities in 1989 following the cessation of navigation pronounced by the Prefect of the Region due to [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought "Drought"). In 1991 operation of the canal was assigned to the administration of _[Voies navigables de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voies\_navigables\_de\_France "Voies navigables de France")_ who remain managers today.

### The canal in the 21st century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: The canal in the 21st century")]

From the end of the 20th century, the canal has offered many activities. It can again play its original role in allowing the transit of boats between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.

#### A canal for tourism and recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: A canal for tourism and recreation")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Bridge_over_Canal_du_Midi.jpg/250px-Bridge_over_Canal_du_Midi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bridge_over_Canal_du_Midi.jpg)

Pleasure-boating has replaced commerce on the Canal du Midi (the hamlet of [Somail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Somail "Le Somail")).

The Canal du Midi is now used primarily by tourists, recreation, and housing.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-75)

It attracts more and more [river tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_tour "Boat tour"), including sailing on chartered boats, restaurant-boats, or [hotel barges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_barge "Hotel barge") such as the [Anjodi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjodi "Anjodi"). Tourism has grown from the 1960s, most significantly from Britain, and then exploded in the 1980s. The canal was featured prominently in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") television series _[Rick Stein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick\_Stein "Rick Stein")'s French Odyssey_ (2005), further publicising the canal to a British audience. Busier than the [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine "Seine"), the canal alone accounts for one-fifth of French river tourism and 80% of passengers are foreigners, primarily Germans, Swiss and British. There are approximately 10,000 boat passages per year through the [Fonséranes locks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonserannes_Lock "Fonserannes Lock"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-ReferenceA-63) with the most traffic at the Argens lock with 11,000 boats carrying an average of five passengers. The canal directly employs about 1,900 people, and the annual economic impact due to the activity of the canal is about 122 million euros.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-chiffre-7)

Navigation of the channel is open from the third Saturday in March to the first week of November. Outside of this period, navigation can be authorized for individuals who have requested it. The winter period is called the "period of unemployment" and allows the completion of all maintenance work.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-76)

The Canal du Midi also allows other sports, mainly in urban areas, such as [rowing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watercraft_rowing "Watercraft rowing"), [canoeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoeing "Canoeing"), [fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing "Fishing"), [cycling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling "Cycling"), [roller-skating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roller-skating "Roller-skating"), and [hiking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiking "Hiking") along the banks. A paved stretch of 50 km (31 mi) from [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") to [Avignonet-Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignonet-Lauragais "Avignonet-Lauragais") and another of 12 km (7.5 mi) between [Béziers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9ziers "Béziers") and [Portiragnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portiragnes "Portiragnes") are particularly suited to cycling and [rollerblading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rollerblading "Rollerblading"). It is possible to cycle the entire Canal des Deux Mers from Sète to Bordeaux. In addition, many barges have been converted to family housing, theatres, exhibition spaces, and restaurants.

#### A canal for water

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: A canal for water")]

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/France_Canal_du_Midi_rigole_de_la_plaine.jpg/250px-France_Canal_du_Midi_rigole_de_la_plaine.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:France_Canal_du_Midi_rigole_de_la_plaine.jpg)

Arrival of the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") in the basin of Naurouze, the main source of water for the Canal du Midi

During the dry season, the canal serves as a reservoir for [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture "Agriculture"). Nearly 700 [irrigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation "Irrigation") pumps are installed along the canal. This is one of the fundamental roles of the canal and one of the reasons for its maintenance by the State since the end of commercial traffic. The canal can irrigate up to 40,000 hectares (150 sq mi) of agricultural land.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-77)

The [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") carries water from the Sor tapped from an offtake at Pont Crouzet for irrigation before emptying into the Canal du Midi. In addition, individual samples are collected from the water on the area between [Revel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revel,_Haute-Garonne "Revel, Haute-Garonne") and the [seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-78) In 1980 the [Lac de la Ganguise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lac_de_la_Ganguise "Lac de la Ganguise") was built near [Castelnaudary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castelnaudary "Castelnaudary") providing a water reserve of 22 million cubic metres. In 2005 the [dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam "Dam") was raised to reach a capacity of 44 million cubic metres.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-79) Near the old basin of Naurouze the Naurouze pumping station helps to regulate the water in the Canal du Midi and the lake. An underground pipe, the gallery of Mandore, provides the Naurouze with additional water from the [Rigole de la plaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigole_de_la_plaine "Rigole de la plaine") to Lake Ganguise. Conversely, during the dry season, Lake Ganguise can supply the Canal du Midi if the water supply of the Rigole de la plaine is not enough.

The canal has also provided a supply of drinking water through the water treatment plants at Picotalen (Picotalen I and Picotalen II) since 1973. They are part of the installations installed by the Institution for Interdepartmental Hydraulic Planning of Montagne Noire (IIAHMN) since its inception in 1948 to meet the water needs of [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais"). The plant supplies water from the Cammazes channel to nearly 185 communes.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-80)

#### The Canal as heritage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canal_du_Midi&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: The Canal as heritage")]

[![Image 27](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f2/BarqueCanalDuMidi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BarqueCanalDuMidi.jpg)

Boat on the Canal du Midi to the south of Toulouse

While the canal was once seen as a tool of production, trade, and commerce it is now considered to be architectural and technical heritage as evidenced by the refusal of the mayor of Toulouse, Pierre Baudis, to allow space on the Canal du Midi to be used for an urban expressway.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-81) It has not been downgraded and remains open for navigation. On 7 December 1996 the channel and a buffer zone of 2,000 km 2 were included in the list of [World Heritage Sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Sites "World Heritage Sites") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO"). In the same year, it was classified under French law as a _Grand Site of France_. This classification was extended to the canals of the plain and the mountain in 1996 and 2001. It caused a very rapid increase in tourist numbers.

Nevertheless, maintenance has not been carried out completely because many players are involved: two [Regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_France "Regions of France"), six [Departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_France "Departments of France"), and local collective authorities. None wish to bear the cost of restoration and do not always dare to launch development programs. _[Platanus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platanus "Platanus")_ (plane trees) is a particular source of problems because their roots destroy the banks and the paved cycle paths and their leaves invade the canal.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-82) In addition they are weakened by disease ([canker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canker "Canker") of _Platanus_). The canal is a heavy heritage to maintain and enhance as the manager of French canals, [Voies navigables de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voies_navigables_de_France "Voies navigables de France") (VNF), specializes in the management and maintenance of [French canals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_canals_in_France "List of canals in France") in a market and commercial economy and not in the tourism market where the Canal du Midi is located. In addition maintenance costs are higher than in a traditional network because of the age of the canal. Also, the operation of the channel generates low levels of earnings. VNF must try to establish local partnerships to develop and maintain the canal[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-rapport_dde-83) since its budget does not allow it to provide the care and supervision of 360 km (220 mi) of canals.

The classification as a World Heritage Site creates an additional level of oversight by the State who must ensure that any changes along the canal and its structures are compatible with the strategic issues of [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO"). However, a report of the General Inspectorate of Architecture and Heritage in 2003 showed that the channel was in very poor condition with many works and infrastructure devaluing its surroundings and suffering from significant housing pressure evidenced by uncontrolled construction, poorly designed facilities that misrepresent the site, and the construction of [marinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marina "Marina") in the ports on the canal. Nevertheless, to respect the uniformity of the canal development and support efforts for improvement, the Canal du Midi remains under the management of VNF under the tutelage of the State who want to create a monitoring mission like the [Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire "Loire") and [Mont-Saint-Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont-Saint-Michel "Mont-Saint-Michel").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-rapport_dde-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_du_Midi#cite_note-84)
