## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Education")]

Aude department in 2008 had 364 primary schools (schools of the first degree) serving 30,771 students. [[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17) Between 2000 and 2007, primary school enrollment steadily increased from 28,331 students to 30,491 students.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17) At secondary level, the department had 31 colleges and 17 public and private high schools for about 23,000 students in 2006.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17)

Education in Aude now includes teaching in the [Occitan language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language").

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Culture")]

### Festivals and traditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Festivals and traditions")]

The [Carnival of Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_of_Limoux "Carnival of Limoux") is an Aude festival which takes place over a period of ten weeks or more. This is one of the longest carnivals in the world. It takes place in the town of [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") on the Place de la République every weekend from mid-January to the end of March. It is characterized by bands in [Pierrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierrot "Pierrot") costumes (known as _les fécos_) accompanied by musicians. In the region around Limoux a major celebration of gastronomy known as _Toques et Clochers_ (literally, "Tall Hats & Steeples') organized by the winegrowers from Sieur d'Arques' takes place over the weekend of [Palm Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Sunday "Palm Sunday"). It permits the sale of a large quantity of wine in order to enhance local patronage.

### Sport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Sport")]

Aude is the land of [rugby league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_league_in_France "Rugby league in France") (rugby à XIII) with the teams of Limoux, Carcassonne and Lézignan among the elite. [Puig Aubert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puig_Aubert "Puig Aubert") (1925–1994) was a famous rugby league player who played with AS Carcassonne. There are numerous amateur rugby league clubs dotted all over the area.

[Rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union_in_France "Rugby union in France") (rugby à XV) is also played in Aude. It appeared early in the twentieth century and the US-Quillan club dominated in the late 1920s. Jean Bourrel won the title in 1929 against [Lézignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan_Sangliers "Lézignan Sangliers"). After the Second World War, the Carcassonne team took the lead. Recently, however, rugby union in the Aude has faced an uphill struggle in a sport that has become both globalized and more professional. The Narbonne team (known as Racing Club Narbonne-Mediterranean) has nevertheless managed to develop in the Pro D2 championship.

Every 15 August, in [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan"), an international cycling competition takes place. This is the oldest of such contests in France.

The [Tour de l'Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_l'Aude_Cycliste_F%C3%A9minin "Tour de l'Aude Cycliste Féminin") is one of the most important female cycling events in the calendar. It generally takes place in May.

### Gastronomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Gastronomy")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG/250px-Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG)

Cassoulet as served at Carcassonne

_[Fréginat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9ginat "Fréginat")_, a traditional type of fricassee of pork from [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res,_Aude "Corbières, Aude"), can be found throughout the department. It is made from pork and pig's liver with a local variety of white beans (Lingots de Castelnaudary) flavoured with garigue herbs. On the coast, eel stew (borrida d’anguilles) is a dish of choice. Finally, the [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet "Cassoulet") of Castelnaudary, made from white beans and sausage, is a typical dish of the [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais").

Other specialties exist such as [oysters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oysters "Oysters") from [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") and [Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate"). [Olive oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_oil "Olive oil") is also very widespread in the Aude and is a speciality of [Bize-Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bize-Minervois "Bize-Minervois"). _Cartagena_ is a [liqueur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liqueur "Liqueur") marketed by some manufacturers. Finally, the [Blanquette de Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanquette_de_Limoux "Blanquette de Limoux") is a sparkling white wine popular in the department whose origin dates back to the sixteenth century.

### Occitan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Occitan")]

[Occitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language") is spoken in the Aude in its Languedoc variant. The language emerged during the [High Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Middle_Ages "High Middle Ages") from the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") used in the south of [Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul").

In Aude, Occitan was rarely used in writing before the 11th century. However, several poets and [troubadours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubadours "Troubadours") such as [Raimon de Miraval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raimon_de_Miraval "Raimon de Miraval") used language based on courtly love[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] in the 12th and 13th centuries. In the 14th and 15th centuries, Occitan was used to draw up local administrative documents. In the 16th century, Occitan was used less than royal French, whose use was made compulsory by the edict of [Villers-Cotterêts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villers-Cotter%C3%AAts "Villers-Cotterêts") in 1539. However, it survived very well among the people until the 19th century, when public schools were established with teaching solely in French.

In the 1970s and the 1980s, new demands were made for the dignity of the language and for its teaching. Occitan speech reached a wider audience and singers like [Claudi Marti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudi_Marti "Claudi Marti"), _Mans de Brèish_, and _La Sauze_ promoted its use.

It was in Aude that the first Occitan radio station broadcast in the region of Languedoc-Roussillon: [Ràdio Lenga](https://web.archive.org/web/20190806092643/http://lengadoc.eu/) (Occitan) at 95.5 FM.

## Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Leucate-La_Franqui_%28Aude%29%2C_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg/250px-Leucate-La_Franqui_%28Aude%29%2C_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leucate-La_Franqui_(Aude),_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg)

Beach at Leucate-La Franqui

Aude is a tourist department with a rich cultural heritage and varied natural sites. Since the 1990s, the Aude has developed the attractiveness of its territory by focusing on the development of the publicity surrounding [Catharism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catharism "Catharism"). The Aude has been named _Cathar Country_ by the General Council to mark the authentic and mysterious nature of the department, especially with its many [Cathar castles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar_castles "Cathar castles").

Tourism is also promoted through a stock of hotel rooms in all categories of 313,500 beds available year-round. Aude estimates the number of tourist overnight stays to be 17.11 million in 2010 with a turnover of 842 million euros providing 5,800 full-time jobs and 9,500 seasonal jobs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-18)

In a very limited section of the Orbiel Valley the department has had occasional pollution problems because of its abandoned gold mines (with mercury and arsenic).

### Overview of tourist areas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Overview of tourist areas")]

[Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") has been restored to much of its [medieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval "Medieval") appearance. [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") is a tourist destination due to its [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") ruins. Other towns and villages worth visiting include [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux"), [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan"), [Lézignan-Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan-Corbi%C3%A8res "Lézignan-Corbières"), [Lagrasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse "Lagrasse"), [Sigean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigean "Sigean") and [Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate").

[Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") lies in the upper Aude valley, 24 km south of [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne"). It is known for its local wine, [Blanquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanquette_de_Limoux "Blanquette de Limoux"), a sparkling white wine which is said to have been the forerunner of Champagne. Limoux hosts an extensive and varied market each Friday.

[Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan") lies 27 km further south in the upper Aude valley and is at the head of the branch railway from [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne").

[Lézignan-Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan-Corbi%C3%A8res "Lézignan-Corbières") lies on the main road between [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") and [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"). It is called the capital of the [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_(AOC) "Corbières (AOC)") and has a Wednesday morning market.

[Lagrasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse "Lagrasse") stands on the [River Orbieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbieu "Orbieu") and has an 8th-century abbey, two bridges, and a well-preserved medieval stone village centre.

[Sigean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigean "Sigean"), 18 km south of [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), lies between the [A9 autoroute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A9_autoroute "A9 autoroute") and the coast and has an African [Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_reserve "Game reserve").

[Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate") is a hilltop village, about 30 km south of Narbonne, which has spread down to the coast where Leucate Plage is a popular beach resort.

The [Corbières Massif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_Massif "Corbières Massif") forms the central part of the department. It is an area of dissected plateaux and escarpments that form an effective barrier to direct road communication, characterized by steep hills, valleys, woodland, and vineyards. It contains several notable [Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar "Cathar") sites including [Quéribus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qu%C3%A9ribus "Quéribus"), [Peyrepertuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyrepertuse "Peyrepertuse"), and [Villerouge-Termenès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villerouge-Termen%C3%A8s "Villerouge-Termenès").

The [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais"), that spreads on both sides of the administrative border between Aude and [Haute-Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute-Garonne "Haute-Garonne"), is a historic and cultural area known since the Middle Ages for its abundant agricultural productions. With [Castelnaudary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castelnaudary "Castelnaudary") as a central and major city, this region is also famous for the role it played during the [Albigensian Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade "Albigensian Crusade") and for its local heritage: Canal du Midi and its springs, abbeys and churches, castles, disk-shaped steles, dovecotes, windmills, bastides, etc.

Wine production is extensive across Aude, and local chateaux and domaines provide free tastings as well as sales of wine and other local produce. With the decline of some local wine production, local government policy is now to attract more tourists to the area, and to assist with this the Corbières area is now labelled on maps and road signs as [Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar "Cathar") country.

### Architectural heritage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Architectural heritage")]

The Aude has about fifteen [bastides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastides "Bastides") which were built after the [Treaty of Meaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Meaux "Treaty of Meaux") in 1229 when the region was attached to the [Capetian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capetian_dynasty "Capetian dynasty") crown of France. The bastide is a type of town based on a grid created in one building project on a greenfield site. The purpose of such construction was to weaken the local lords and attract people to new economic centres. These bastides came into competition with fortified villages based on ecclesiastical or seigneurial power. [Chalabre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalabre "Chalabre"), [Camps-sur-l'Agly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camps-sur-l'Agly "Camps-sur-l'Agly") and the Bastide Saint-Louis in Carcassonne are examples of bastides in the Aude.

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg/250px-190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg)

Puilaurens Castle

The department has many castles that have been developed by the General Council of the Aude to stimulate tourism. The fortresses are often located on rocky peaks, such as the castles of Quéribus and [Lastours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lastours "Lastours"), which gave them a strategic position. The city of Carcassonne was the logistical hub of the country at the time of conflict with the Kingdom of [Aragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aragon "Aragon").

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Fontfroide%2C_Arbeitshof.jpg/250px-Fontfroide%2C_Arbeitshof.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fontfroide,_Arbeitshof.jpg)

[Fontfroide Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontfroide_Abbey "Fontfroide Abbey"), Tourism highlight of Aude

Many abbeys exist throughout the department of Aude. The best known are [Fontfroide Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontfroide_Abbey "Fontfroide Abbey"), [Lagrasse Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse_Abbey "Lagrasse Abbey"), the abbey of Sainte-Marie [Villelongue-d'Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villelongue-d'Aude "Villelongue-d'Aude"), and the Abbey of [Saint-Hilaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Hilaire,_Aude "Saint-Hilaire, Aude").

[Narbonne Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne_Cathedral "Narbonne Cathedral") is a remarkable Gothic cathedral and remains unfinished. It is a symbol of the French presence in [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc") in the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages").

### Caving

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Caving")]

Aude has many caves suitable for [speleological exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speleology "Speleology"). The _Pays de Sault_ consists of one of the largest limestone areas of the Pyrenees. This geology lends itself to the formation of cavities and there are many 'barrencs' (the local name for [Pit caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit_cave "Pit cave")). This plateau is home to a cave, the TM71, which is a superb cavity classified as a natural reserve since 1987. This is unique in France.

Other natural cavities of the Aude contain [concretions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concretions "Concretions") like the Pit cave of [Cabrespine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabrespine "Cabrespine"), the Aguzou Grotto, and the grotto of [Limousis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limousis "Limousis"). The latter contains the largest block of [aragonite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aragonite "Aragonite") yet discovered. In the Massif of Corbières on the plateau of Lacamp there are cavities formed by [detrital rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detritus_(geology) "Detritus (geology)") ([marls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marls "Marls"), [clays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay "Clay") and [puddingstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puddingstone_(rock) "Puddingstone (rock)")) carved by [erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erosion "Erosion").

## Arts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Arts")]

### Cinema

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Cinema")]

The diversity of the landscape, its authenticity, and the uniqueness of its monuments have attracted many filmmakers. Thus, the city of [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") has been the setting for many films. The excellent state of preservation of this city offers an outstanding setting for historical films. In 1908 filmmakers abandoned scenery on canvas and [Louis Feuillade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Feuillade "Louis Feuillade") filmed in front of the city towers for the _Return of the cross_, _Engagement oath_, and _Enchanted guitar_. In 1924 major films were produced such as _[Le Miracle des Loups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Miracle\_des\_loups\_(1924\_film) "Le Miracle des loups (1924 film)")_ by [Raymond Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Bernard_(filmmaker) "Raymond Bernard (filmmaker)"). In 1928 for the two thousandth anniversary of the city of Carcassonne, [Jean Renoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Renoir "Jean Renoir") made _Le Tournoi dans la cité_. In 1965 the city of Carcassonne appeared in _[The Sucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sucker "The Sucker")_ by [Gerard Oury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Oury "Gerard Oury"). In 1968 _[The Little Bather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Little\_Bather "The Little Bather")_ by [Robert Dhéry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Dh%C3%A9ry "Robert Dhéry") (with [Louis de Funès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_de_Fun%C3%A8s "Louis de Funès") and [Michel Galabru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Galabru "Michel Galabru")) shot at _Cabanes de Fleury_ (at the mouth of the Aude).

More recently, the Count's castle in the city was the setting for _[The Visitors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Visitors\_(1972\_film) "The Visitors (1972 film)")_ by [Jean-Marie Poire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Marie_Poire "Jean-Marie Poire") in 1972, while the [Château de Puivert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Puivert "Château de Puivert") was used in _La Passion Béatrice_ by [Bertrand Tavernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand_Tavernier "Bertrand Tavernier") in 1987, and _[The Ninth Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ninth\_Gate "The Ninth Gate")_ by [Roman Polanski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Polanski "Roman Polanski") in 1999. The Beach at [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") is present in [Betty Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Blue "Betty Blue") by [Jean-Jacques Beineix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Jacques_Beineix "Jean-Jacques Beineix").

### Painters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=42 "Edit section: Painters")]

As for the cinema, it is the city of Carcassonne which attracts the greatest painters. [Jacques Ourtal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Ourtal?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jacques Ourtal (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques%20Ourtal "fr:Jacques Ourtal")] is the one who painted most of the city in trying to depict the city in different eras. Originally from [Fontiers-Cabardès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontiers-Cabard%C3%A8s "Fontiers-Cabardès"), the Aude painter _Eugène Pech_ has created paintings of the city many times which are today scattered in various public and private collections. The four eras of the city can still be found in settings for "The City Hall".

Another Aude artist, [Marie-Louise Petiet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Petiet "Marie Petiet"), is known for her transcriptions of scenes of popular life such as _La marchande d'oranges_ (The Orange Seller) or _La jeune fille aux oies_ (The young girl and the geese). Several of her works are visible at the Petiet Museum in Limoux. _Les blanchisseuses_ (The Laundresses) depicting a laundry lesson is particularly remarkable and well-known. Finally, [Paul Sibra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sibra "Paul Sibra"), an expert in landscape-painting, nicknamed "_le peintre du Lauragais_", produced thousands of paintings and drawings of scenes from or based on the rural life of the people of _Lauragais_ in the 1940s.

[Achille Laugé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille_Laug%C3%A9?action=edit&redlink=1 "Achille Laugé (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "fr:Achille Laugé"); [de](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "de:Achille Laugé"); [it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "it:Achille Laugé")] (born 1861 in Arzens, died 1944 in Cailhau), misunderstood because of his pointillist technique, was able to show the dawning of spring especially with the [broom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broom_(shrub) "Broom (shrub)") and [almond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almond "Almond") trees in bloom.

Another artist, [Lina Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lina_Bill?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lina Bill (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lina%20Bill "fr:Lina Bill")] (real name Louis Bonnot), born at [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") in 1855 and died in [Avignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon "Avignon") in 1936, painted Provence and the Mediterranean (museums of [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne"), and the [Musée d'Orsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mus%C3%A9e_d'Orsay "Musée d'Orsay") in Paris).

**Aude** ([/oʊ d/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_OHD_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); French:[[od]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/9/9d/LL-Q150_%28fra%29-GrandCelinien-Aude.wav/LL-Q150_%28fra%29-GrandCelinien-Aude.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LL-Q150_(fra)-GrandCelinien-Aude.wav "File:LL-Q150 (fra)-GrandCelinien-Aude.wav"); Occitan:[[ˈawðe]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Occitan "Help:IPA/Occitan")) is a [department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_France "Departments of France") in southern France, located in [Occitania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitania_(administrative_region) "Occitania (administrative region)") and named after the river [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(river) "Aude (river)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-sandre-3) The departmental council also calls it "[Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catharism "Catharism") Country" (French: _Pays cathare_) after a group of religious dissidents active in the 12th to 14th centuries.

Its [prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefectures_in_France "Prefectures in France") is [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") and its [subprefectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subprefectures_in_France "Subprefectures in France") are [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") and [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"). As of 2023, it had a population of 379,648.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-pophist-4) Aude is a frequent feminine French given name in Francophone countries, deriving initially from Aude or Oda, a wife of Bertrand, [Duke of Aquitaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_of_Aquitaine "Duke of Aquitaine"), and mother of Eudo, brother of Saint [Hubertus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubertus "Hubertus").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Aude was the name of [Roland's fiancée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(character) "Aude (character)") in the [_chansons de geste_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanson_de_geste "Chanson de geste").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

### Location

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Location")]

Aude is located between the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea") and the [Pyrenees Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees").

It is part of the current region of [Occitanie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitania_(administrative_region) "Occitania (administrative region)"). It is surrounded by the departments of [Pyrénées-Orientales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es-Orientales "Pyrénées-Orientales"), [Ariège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ari%C3%A8ge_(department) "Ariège (department)"), [Haute-Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute-Garonne "Haute-Garonne"), [Tarn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarn_(department) "Tarn (department)"), and [Hérault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rault "Hérault"), with the [Golfe du Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golfe_du_Lion "Golfe du Lion") on the east.

Natural regions of the Aude

The countryside in this department falls into several [natural regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_region "Natural region"):

*   1 – [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais")
*   2 – [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire")
*   3 – [Cabardès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabard%C3%A8s "Cabardès")
*   4 – [Carcassonnais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne")
*   5 – [Razès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raz%C3%A8s "Razès")
*   6 – [Quercorb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercorb "Quercorb")
*   7 – [Pays de Sault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pays_de_Sault "Pays de Sault")
*   8 – [Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minervois "Minervois")
*   9 – [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res,_Aude "Corbières, Aude")
*   10 – [Narbonnais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonnais "Narbonnais")

### Landscapes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Landscapes")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Quillan.jpg/250px-Quillan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quillan.jpg)

Mountain landscape in the [Razès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raz%C3%A8s "Razès") at [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan")

Each natural region of the Aude has its own particular landscape. In the east, lagoons or coastal lakes separate land and sea. These were formed by accumulations of sediments carried down by the rivers Aude, [Orb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orb_(river) "Orb (river)") and [Hérault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9rault_(river) "Hérault (river)"). There are many such lakes of brackish water. This environment is demanding for flora and fauna, as it suffers from the rigours of sea, sun, dryness and floods. [Halophile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halophile "Halophile") (i.e., salt-loving) plants grow there. The area is also noted for the pink [flamingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo "Flamingo") and the white [stilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stilt "Stilt").

Inland to the west, [shrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maquis_shrubland "Maquis shrubland") and [scrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrigue "Garrigue") dominate the landscape of the drylands of the Aude and the [Corbières Massif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_Massif "Corbières Massif"). This landscape is the result of forest clearance, maintained by the raising of livestock. The flora is varied and characterized by many species of [orchids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchids "Orchids"). The Sault countryside is dominated by [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beech "Beech") groves and [fir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fir "Fir") plantations up to the mountains. These forests are known for their [mushrooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom "Mushroom"), and have a rich flora and fauna, including the [Pyrenean lily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenean_lily "Pyrenean lily"), the [euproctis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euproctis "Euproctis") moth and [horsetail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsetail "Horsetail") of the woods.

To the north and west, the Black Mountain country is made up of forests of [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak "Oak") and [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beech "Beech"). The Lauragais is a wooded landscape where grain farming has shaped the hills. There are bodies of water like the [Lac de la Ganguise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lac_de_la_Ganguise "Lac de la Ganguise"). Finally, the high valley of the Aude, otherwise called the Razès, consists of a [riparian forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riparian_forest "Riparian forest") made of beech, [alder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alder "Alder"), [poplar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populus "Populus") or [ash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraxinus "Fraxinus"). It includes some [peatlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peatlands "Peatlands") that are very rare in southern France.

### Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Geology")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Aude_%28flume%29.png/250px-Aude_%28flume%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aude_(flume).png)

Relief map with some main towns

The landscapes of Aude can be explained by its geology. In the south, there are [sedimentary rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rocks "Sedimentary rocks") folded during the formation of the Pyrenees. To the north and centre of Aude, the sedimentary rocks are less folded. At the extreme east, near the Mediterranean, the rocks are carved by normal collapse [faults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_(geology) "Fault (geology)") which are due to the opening of the Golfe du Lion. The limestone [Massif de la Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape "Massif de la Clape") runs along the entire coast from Gruissan to Saint-Pierre-la-Mer, and has to be crossed to go from Narbonne to Narbonne-Plage.

In the north, the Black Mountain and Minervois consist of [schist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schist "Schist") and [marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marble "Marble"), forming the southern edge of the [Massif Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_Central "Massif Central"). These ancient rocks are over 300 million years old and were deformed by the formation of the [Hercynian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variscan_orogeny "Variscan orogeny") chain. The Montagne d'Alaric ([Alaric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaric_II "Alaric II")'s Mountain)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-5) near Carcassonne is an [antiform fold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticline "Anticline") in the shape of a vault and made of [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone").

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Climate")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Port_and_lighthouse_overnight_storm_with_lightning_in_Port-la-Nouvelle.jpg/250px-Port_and_lighthouse_overnight_storm_with_lightning_in_Port-la-Nouvelle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Port_and_lighthouse_overnight_storm_with_lightning_in_Port-la-Nouvelle.jpg)

Lightning during an autumn storm off the coast of [Port-la-Nouvelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-la-Nouvelle "Port-la-Nouvelle").

Aude is under the influence of a Mediterranean climate.

The autumn is characterized by violent and short storms. The summer is often hot and dry, which is favorable to the culture of the vine and the olive-trees. Yet, the department has several contrasts in climate: In the north, the Montagne Noire and, in the south, the Pays de Sault, have a mountainous climate with temperatures sometimes very low in winter. In the west, the climate is under Aquitaine influence with heavier precipitation, while in the east the climate is purely Mediterranean. In the centre, in the Limouxin, Carcassonnais and Razès areas, the climate is known as intermediary with significant exposure to winds. The winds are often present in Aude. It is one of the windiest French departments, with 300 to 350 days of wind per year. This phenomenon is due mostly to the variations in relief north and south which create a kind of corridor.

In the north-west blows the [Cers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cers_(wind) "Cers (wind)"), called Tramontane in Provence, which is a ground wind. It is a dry, somewhat violent wind and cold in winter. In the south-east blows the Autan, locally called the [Marin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_(wind) "Marin (wind)"), which is hot and wet and comes from the sea.

These regular winds made it possible to install an industrial park of [wind turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_turbine "Wind turbine"), as in the area of Avignonet-Lauragais.

### Hydrography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Hydrography")]

The drainage system of Aude is dominated by its river of the same name. The river rises at the Roc d'Aude and passes through the [Matemale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matemale "Matemale") and [Puyvalador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puyvalador "Puyvalador") dams on the [Capcir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capcir "Capcir") plateau at 1500m, then crosses the department from south to north across Axat, Limoux, and Quillan following the upper valley of the Aude. At Carcassonne, the river changes direction toward the Mediterranean Sea to the east, where it empties near [Fleury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleury,_Aude "Fleury, Aude").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: History")]

### Prehistory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Prehistory")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Homme_de_Tautavel.jpg/250px-Homme_de_Tautavel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Homme_de_Tautavel.jpg)

Skull of [Tautavel Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tautavel_Man "Tautavel Man") discovered at [Tautavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tautavel "Tautavel"), not far from Aude

Hammers and worked tools have been found on the hill of Grazailles at Carcassonne, dating from between 690,000 and 300,000 years ago. Most interesting is the skull of [Tautavel Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tautavel_Man "Tautavel Man"), discovered in 1971 by [Henry de Lumley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_de_Lumley "Henry de Lumley") in the commune of [Tautavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tautavel "Tautavel") in the [Pyrénées-Orientales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es-Orientales "Pyrénées-Orientales") department.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-9) It is the oldest-known skull in Europe. It dates from about 450,000 years BC. It is likely that Tautavel Man lived in all of this region.

### Roman Era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Roman Era")]

The [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Republic "Roman Republic"), led by the consul-general [Domitius Ahenobarbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnaeus_Domitius_Ahenobarbus_(consul_122_BC) "Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus (consul 122 BC)"), first occupied the [oppidum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppidum "Oppidum") of Montlaurès in 118 BC, a few kilometres to the north of [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"). This became the provincial capital and a very active mercantile port. The position was strategically important since it stood at the crossroads of two [Roman roads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_roads "Roman roads"), the [Via Aquitania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_Aquitania "Via Aquitania") and the [Via Domitia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_Domitia "Via Domitia"), as well as by the sea near the mouth of the river [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(river) "Aude (river)"). [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") became Latin in 30 BC with the creation of numerous grain farms. For almost two centuries, Aude enjoyed peace and strong economic growth.

### Barbarian invasions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Barbarian invasions")]

The [Visigoths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visigoths "Visigoths") invaded the area in 435 AD at a time when [Flavius Aetius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavius_Aetius "Flavius Aetius"), the Roman senator, was busy suppressing the [Bagaudes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagaudes "Bagaudes"), who were brigands or lawless types in central and northern Gaul. Roman authority was restored until 462. In 507, the victory of [Clovis I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clovis_I "Clovis I") at the [battle of Vouillé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Vouill%C3%A9 "Battle of Vouillé") permitted him to conquer [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") and [Aquitaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquitaine "Aquitaine"). However, he could not recover the Aude territory, which, thanks to the help of the King of the [Ostrogoths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostrogoths "Ostrogoths"), remained in the hands of the Visigoths. His troops defeated Clovis's son in 508. The region was part of [Septimania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Septimania "Septimania"), so called because it was composed of seven [bishoprics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_see "Episcopal see") that the Visigoth kings had established there: [Elne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elne "Elne"), [Agde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agde "Agde"), [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), [Lodève](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lod%C3%A8ve "Lodève"), [Béziers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9ziers "Béziers"), [Maguelonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maguelonne "Maguelonne"), and [Nîmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%AEmes "Nîmes"). Septimania covered the Aude but also the whole region of Languedoc-Roussillon.

### Middle Ages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Middle Ages")]

In 817, [Louis le Débonnaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_le_D%C3%A9bonnaire "Louis le Débonnaire") detached Carcassès and [Razès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raz%C3%A8s "Razès") from Septimania to reunite them with the marquisate of [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") and the kingdom of [Aquitaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquitaine "Aquitaine"). The first Count of Carcassonne was Oliba from the family of the [Counts of Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_of_Barcelona "Count of Barcelona"). He established himself in 819. Razès was another county that was formed by an archbishop of Narbonne who had been chased from his town by the [Saracens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saracens "Saracens"). He had transferred his episcopal seat to Razès and had procured the honours of the feudal title for the area. Narbonne formed a third county. Thus, in the ninth century, the département of Aude consisted of three counties: Carcassonne, Razès and Narbonne. In 880, the [County of Razès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Raz%C3%A8s "County of Razès") was united by marriage to that of Carcassonne, never to be separated.

### Catharism in Aude

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Catharism in Aude")]

In the 13th century, the region saw the development of [Catharism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catharism "Catharism"): a [dualistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dualistic_cosmology "Dualistic cosmology") Christian sect with similarities to [Gnosticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnosticism "Gnosticism"). This religion was very quickly judged as heretical by the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church"). Faced with its growing strength in the counties of Carcassonne and Toulouse, [Pope Innocent III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Innocent_III "Pope Innocent III") in 1209 declared a [crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade "Albigensian Crusade") against the [Albigensians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensians "Albigensians"). The barons of the north united to form an army under the command of [Simon de Montfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_de_Montfort,_5th_Earl_of_Leicester "Simon de Montfort, 5th Earl of Leicester"). Whereas the count of Toulouse [Raymond VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_VI "Raymond VI") received absolution, the Count of Carcassonne confronted the army alone. The city of Carcassonne became the refuge of numerous Cathars.

### The Protestant crisis and economic expansion of the department

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: The Protestant crisis and economic expansion of the department")]

In 1561, religious troubles again arose at [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") in the form of a Protestant crisis. Duke [Henri I de Montmorency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_I_de_Montmorency "Henri I de Montmorency"), the Governor of the [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc"), joined the [Reformed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_tradition "Reformed tradition") side in 1574. On the Catholic side, the Duke [Anne de Joyeuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_de_Joyeuse "Anne de Joyeuse") became head of the Catholic League. In September 1632, [Henri II de Montmorency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_II_de_Montmorency "Henri II de Montmorency") fought against the royal troops at the Battle of [Castelnaudary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castelnaudary "Castelnaudary") and was defeated. He was condemned to death and executed at Toulouse.

### The creation of the department

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: The creation of the department")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Carte_du_d%C3%A9partement_de_l%27Aude_-_1790-1793.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Carte_du_d%C3%A9partement_de_l%27Aude_-_1790-1793.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carte_du_d%C3%A9partement_de_l'Aude_-_1790-1793.tif)

Aude in 1790

The present department is one of the original 83 departments created by the [Constituent Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Assembly "Constituent Assembly") during the [French Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution") on 4 March 1790. It was created from part of the [former province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_France "Provinces of France") of [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc"). Administrative divisions were amended by the Act of 28 [Pluviôse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pluvi%C3%B4se "Pluviôse") of Year 8, which created four arrondissements (reduced to three by Premier [Raymond Poincaré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Poincar%C3%A9 "Raymond Poincaré") in 1926) and reduced the number of cantons from 45 to 31.

### The 20th century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: The 20th century")]

The Aude enjoyed strong wine production whilst at the same time the grain farmers of [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais") faced great difficulties. However, the department suffered from overproduction and a slump in sales of wine. In 1907 the crisis produced a [winemakers' revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907_Languedoc_Winemaker's_Revolt?action=edit&redlink=1 "1907 Languedoc Winemaker's Revolt (page does not exist)"). This led to the establishment of many [Winemaking cooperatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winemaking_cooperative "Winemaking cooperative") in Aude from 1909.

### Agriculture and fisheries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Agriculture and fisheries")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Port_Leucate_%28Aude%29%2C_view_over_Leucate.jpg/250px-Port_Leucate_%28Aude%29%2C_view_over_Leucate.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Port_Leucate_(Aude),_view_over_Leucate.jpg)

Entry to the port of [Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate")

Aude is an agricultural area dominated by vineyards. In the east are the wines of [Corbieres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_AOC "Corbières AOC") and [La Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Clape "La Clape"), in the centre are [Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minervois "Minervois") and Côtes de Malepère, and in the south [Limoux wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux_wine "Limoux wine"). In [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais") grain is predominant, whereas in the [Montagne Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montagne_Noire "Montagne Noire") only [sheep farming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep_farming "Sheep farming") is possible. More recently there has been an increase in cultivation of [olive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive "Olive") trees for their oil.

[Port-la-Nouvelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-la-Nouvelle "Port-la-Nouvelle") is the biggest fishing port in the department followed by [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan"). In 1996 there were 127 vessels in Aude including 75 in Port-la-Nouvelle and 52 in Gruissan.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-11) These vessels were as follows:

*   [Fishing trawlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_trawler "Fishing trawler"): 19 in Port-la-Nouvelle
*   tuna boats: 2 in Port-la-Nouvelle
*   small craft: 106 including 54 in Port-La-Nouvelle and 52 in Gruissan

Small craft are recreational boats such as dinghies with one man fishing a lake or motor launches with up to three people fishing in coastal waters. About 85% of small craft are intended for lake fishing as in the [Étang de Thau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tang_de_Thau "Étang de Thau").

### Viticulture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Viticulture")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Vignoble_Map_Aude.svg/500px-Vignoble_Map_Aude.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vignoble_Map_Aude.svg)

Map of wine growing areas of the Aude

[Viticulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viticulture "Viticulture") is the main economic activity of the department due to its rich and varied soils. It was the Greeks who established vineyards in Aude and the Romans who determined the rights of exploitation. The first vines were planted in [Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minervois "Minervois") in the 1st century.

But the grapes and wines were not consumer products or self-sufficient for many years. Cereals and olive trees dominated the fertile plains of Aude. It was at the beginning of the 19th century that the wine industry developed in Aude and the rest of Languedoc-Roussillon. Wine then became a consumer product. Higher output was needed and vineyards replaced cereals on the plains. There was an initial period of prosperity to 1850 before [phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylloxera "Phylloxera") appeared towards 1870. At the end of the 19th century, Aude experienced a second period of prosperity but there was a wine crisis triggered in 1901 because of over-production, fraud, and slumping sales. It reached its peak during the winemakers revolt in 1907. The wine growers regrouped themselves into [winemaking cooperatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winemaking_cooperative "Winemaking cooperative") to prevent fraud and deception. In 1919 then in 1935, a law of [AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e "Appellation d'origine contrôlée") was adopted under the leadership of Jean Capus. The [INAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INAO "INAO") was set up as a body to control the application of the new laws.

After the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), the vineyards were revitalized and the region saw a mass of viticulture. The wine was produced in large quantities and satisfied a very demanding population. The product was supplied in large quantities at very low prices. In 1970 the market evolved replacing demand for quantity with demand for quality and causing a second wine crisis. Many events, negotiations, and attacks paralyzed the region and the economy. Emile Pouytès and the CRS Joel le Gof died at [Montredon-des-Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montredon-des-Corbi%C3%A8res "Montredon-des-Corbières") on 4 March 1976 during this crisis. A large change in the Aude viticulture business started with a reorganization of the profession and the wine-growing region. Quality had to become the mark of wine from Aude.

The rich and varied soil of Aude together with abundant sunshine enables Aude to produce quality wines. Many wines emanate from the department, ranging in quality from [table wines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table_wine "Table wine") to [AOCs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e "Appellation d'origine contrôlée"), passing through [vins de pays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vins_de_pays "Vins de pays") and [VDQS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VDQS "VDQS").

There are seven main areas of production:

*   [Cabardès AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabard%C3%A8s_AOC "Cabardès AOC") (1),
*   [Corbières AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_AOC "Corbières AOC") (6),
*   [Côtes Malepère](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_appellations_in_Languedoc-Roussillon "List of appellations in Languedoc-Roussillon") AOC near Carcassonne (2),
*   [Coteaux du Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_appellations_in_Languedoc-Roussillon "List of appellations in Languedoc-Roussillon") on the plain of Narbonnais (5),
*   [Fitou AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitou_AOC "Fitou AOC") (7),
*   [Limoux wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux_wine "Limoux wine") (3),
*   [Minervois AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minervois_AOC "Minervois AOC") (4).

These areas produce different wines such as _[Blanquette de Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux\_wine "Limoux wine")_, [Chardonnay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chardonnay "Chardonnay") and sparkling wine from Limoux, _[La Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Clape "La Clape")_, [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res,_Aude "Corbières, Aude"), [Fitou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitou "Fitou"), and [Cabardès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabard%C3%A8s "Cabardès").

### Industry and energy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Industry and energy")]

Industrial activity is strong in the upper valley of the Aude. It has been especially prominent around [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") since the late nineteenth century; and the [Lafarge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafarge_(company) "Lafarge (company)") brick plant there is still booming.

Since the 1970s, however, the Aude has seen a rapid decline in its traditional industries such as shoe and hat making. More recent activity is mostly centred around [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), particularly [dock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dock_(maritime) "Dock (maritime)") facilities and [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum "Petroleum") depots in [Port-la-Nouvelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port-la-Nouvelle "Port-la-Nouvelle").

From 1889, the high valley of Aude became increasingly important in generating [hydroelectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroelectric "Hydroelectric") power. Aude was the first department in France to transmit such power, from its plants at [Alet-les-Bains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alet-les-Bains "Alet-les-Bains") and [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan"). Joachim Estrade established the first electricity company in France, the Southern Power Transmission Company (SMTF), in 1901. Its plant at [Axat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axat "Axat")-Saint-Georges supplied the cities of Carcassonne and Narbonne at 20 [kilovolts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilovolts "Kilovolts").

Today Aude is the leading department in France for the number of wind turbines installed. There are 113 in operation. They produce some 91 [megawatts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megawatts "Megawatts"), which is the domestic electricity consumption of about 100,000 people.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-12) With the proliferation of these machines, the prefecture is seeking to establish with stakeholders a charter of good conduct for wind turbines.

### Crafts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Crafts")]

[Crafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crafts "Crafts") are very well represented in Aude with 14.6% of the population involved. ## Demography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Demography")]

The inhabitants of Aude are known as _Audois_. Its population increases, due to positive migration balance, offset by slightly negative natural growth.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-14)

Aude is predominantly rural with a population density of 62 inhabitants per km 2, which is about half of the national average. The two main cities, Carcassonne and Narbonne, are medium-sized cities comprising only one third of the inhabitants of the department.

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Transport")]

Two major roads cross the Aude. From west to east the [A61 autoroute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A61_autoroute "A61 autoroute") (Autoroute des Deux Mers) connects [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") and [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse "Toulouse") via [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne"). From north to south, following the Mediterranean coast, the [A9 autoroute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A9_autoroute "A9 autoroute") links [Montpellier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montpellier "Montpellier") with Spain.

The rail network follows the same route as the road network. It is a low speed system, but a project is under way to build a fast line to Spain as part of the [Trans-European Rail network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-European_Rail_network "Trans-European Rail network").

In terms of air travel, the department is served by [Carcassonne Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne_Airport "Carcassonne Airport") which provides direct routes some European destinations. The nearest major airport is [Toulouse–Blagnac Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse%E2%80%93Blagnac_Airport "Toulouse–Blagnac Airport") which is mostly used by air travellers from the department.

Finally, Aude is crossed by the Canal du Midi which is a major waterway that allows tourists to pass from the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea. It comes into the west of Aude at [Seuil de Naurouze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuil_de_Naurouze "Seuil de Naurouze") then joins the Mediterranean at [Sète](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A8te "Sète").

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Politics")]

See also: [Departmental Council of Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departmental_Council_of_Aude "Departmental Council of Aude")

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Arrondissements_et_cantons_de_l%27Aude.svg/500px-Arrondissements_et_cantons_de_l%27Aude.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Arrondissements_et_cantons_de_l'Aude.svg)

Map of arrondissements and cantons of Aude

The people of Aude expressed [royalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royalist "Royalist") opinions until the end of the [Bourbon Restoration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Restoration_in_France "Bourbon Restoration in France"). In 1830 [republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism "Republicanism") ideas began to develop and made this department a bastion of the [left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-wing_politics "Left-wing politics"). This growth is symbolized by two men, [Armand Barbès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armand_Barb%C3%A8s "Armand Barbès") and Theophile Marcou. Armand Barbès is a symbol of the struggle for a [social democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democratic "Social democratic") Republic.

It was in Aude that [François Mitterrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Mitterrand "François Mitterrand") had his highest score in the 1981 presidential election with just over 63% of the vote.

Only affluent coastal areas surrounding [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") and the department's prefecture, [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") give consideration to the right.

The President of the Departmental Council is Hélène Sandragné of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France) "Socialist Party (France)").

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Education")]

Aude department in 2008 had 364 primary schools (schools of the first degree) serving 30,771 students. [[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17) Between 2000 and 2007, primary school enrollment steadily increased from 28,331 students to 30,491 students.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17) At secondary level, the department had 31 colleges and 17 public and private high schools for about 23,000 students in 2006.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-Montpelier-17)

Education in Aude now includes teaching in the [Occitan language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language").

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Culture")]

### Festivals and traditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Festivals and traditions")]

The [Carnival of Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_of_Limoux "Carnival of Limoux") is an Aude festival which takes place over a period of ten weeks or more. This is one of the longest carnivals in the world. It takes place in the town of [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") on the Place de la République every weekend from mid-January to the end of March. It is characterized by bands in [Pierrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierrot "Pierrot") costumes (known as _les fécos_) accompanied by musicians. In the region around Limoux a major celebration of gastronomy known as _Toques et Clochers_ (literally, "Tall Hats & Steeples') organized by the winegrowers from Sieur d'Arques' takes place over the weekend of [Palm Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Sunday "Palm Sunday"). It permits the sale of a large quantity of wine in order to enhance local patronage.

### Sport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Sport")]

Aude is the land of [rugby league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_league_in_France "Rugby league in France") (rugby à XIII) with the teams of Limoux, Carcassonne and Lézignan among the elite. [Puig Aubert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puig_Aubert "Puig Aubert") (1925–1994) was a famous rugby league player who played with AS Carcassonne. There are numerous amateur rugby league clubs dotted all over the area.

[Rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union_in_France "Rugby union in France") (rugby à XV) is also played in Aude. It appeared early in the twentieth century and the US-Quillan club dominated in the late 1920s. Jean Bourrel won the title in 1929 against [Lézignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan_Sangliers "Lézignan Sangliers"). After the Second World War, the Carcassonne team took the lead. Recently, however, rugby union in the Aude has faced an uphill struggle in a sport that has become both globalized and more professional. The Narbonne team (known as Racing Club Narbonne-Mediterranean) has nevertheless managed to develop in the Pro D2 championship.

Every 15 August, in [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan"), an international cycling competition takes place. This is the oldest of such contests in France.

The [Tour de l'Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_l'Aude_Cycliste_F%C3%A9minin "Tour de l'Aude Cycliste Féminin") is one of the most important female cycling events in the calendar. It generally takes place in May.

### Gastronomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Gastronomy")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG/250px-Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cassoulet_Carcassonne_FRA_001.JPG)

Cassoulet as served at Carcassonne

_[Fréginat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9ginat "Fréginat")_, a traditional type of fricassee of pork from [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res,_Aude "Corbières, Aude"), can be found throughout the department. It is made from pork and pig's liver with a local variety of white beans (Lingots de Castelnaudary) flavoured with garigue herbs. On the coast, eel stew (borrida d’anguilles) is a dish of choice. Finally, the [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet "Cassoulet") of Castelnaudary, made from white beans and sausage, is a typical dish of the [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais").

Other specialties exist such as [oysters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oysters "Oysters") from [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") and [Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate"). [Olive oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_oil "Olive oil") is also very widespread in the Aude and is a speciality of [Bize-Minervois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bize-Minervois "Bize-Minervois"). _Cartagena_ is a [liqueur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liqueur "Liqueur") marketed by some manufacturers. Finally, the [Blanquette de Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanquette_de_Limoux "Blanquette de Limoux") is a sparkling white wine popular in the department whose origin dates back to the sixteenth century.

### Occitan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Occitan")]

[Occitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language") is spoken in the Aude in its Languedoc variant. The language emerged during the [High Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Middle_Ages "High Middle Ages") from the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") used in the south of [Gaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul "Gaul").

In Aude, Occitan was rarely used in writing before the 11th century. However, several poets and [troubadours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubadours "Troubadours") such as [Raimon de Miraval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raimon_de_Miraval "Raimon de Miraval") used language based on courtly love[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] in the 12th and 13th centuries. In the 14th and 15th centuries, Occitan was used to draw up local administrative documents. In the 16th century, Occitan was used less than royal French, whose use was made compulsory by the edict of [Villers-Cotterêts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villers-Cotter%C3%AAts "Villers-Cotterêts") in 1539. However, it survived very well among the people until the 19th century, when public schools were established with teaching solely in French.

In the 1970s and the 1980s, new demands were made for the dignity of the language and for its teaching. Occitan speech reached a wider audience and singers like [Claudi Marti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudi_Marti "Claudi Marti"), _Mans de Brèish_, and _La Sauze_ promoted its use.

It was in Aude that the first Occitan radio station broadcast in the region of Languedoc-Roussillon: [Ràdio Lenga](https://web.archive.org/web/20190806092643/http://lengadoc.eu/) (Occitan) at 95.5 FM.

## Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Leucate-La_Franqui_%28Aude%29%2C_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg/250px-Leucate-La_Franqui_%28Aude%29%2C_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leucate-La_Franqui_(Aude),_view_from_the_cliffs.jpg)

Beach at Leucate-La Franqui

Aude is a tourist department with a rich cultural heritage and varied natural sites. Since the 1990s, the Aude has developed the attractiveness of its territory by focusing on the development of the publicity surrounding [Catharism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catharism "Catharism"). The Aude has been named _Cathar Country_ by the General Council to mark the authentic and mysterious nature of the department, especially with its many [Cathar castles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar_castles "Cathar castles").

Tourism is also promoted through a stock of hotel rooms in all categories of 313,500 beds available year-round. Aude estimates the number of tourist overnight stays to be 17.11 million in 2010 with a turnover of 842 million euros providing 5,800 full-time jobs and 9,500 seasonal jobs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude_(department)#cite_note-18)

In a very limited section of the Orbiel Valley the department has had occasional pollution problems because of its abandoned gold mines (with mercury and arsenic).

### Overview of tourist areas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Overview of tourist areas")]

[Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") has been restored to much of its [medieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval "Medieval") appearance. [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne") is a tourist destination due to its [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") ruins. Other towns and villages worth visiting include [Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux"), [Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan"), [Lézignan-Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan-Corbi%C3%A8res "Lézignan-Corbières"), [Lagrasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse "Lagrasse"), [Sigean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigean "Sigean") and [Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate").

[Limoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limoux "Limoux") lies in the upper Aude valley, 24 km south of [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne"). It is known for its local wine, [Blanquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanquette_de_Limoux "Blanquette de Limoux"), a sparkling white wine which is said to have been the forerunner of Champagne. Limoux hosts an extensive and varied market each Friday.

[Quillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillan "Quillan") lies 27 km further south in the upper Aude valley and is at the head of the branch railway from [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne").

[Lézignan-Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A9zignan-Corbi%C3%A8res "Lézignan-Corbières") lies on the main road between [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") and [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"). It is called the capital of the [Corbières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_(AOC) "Corbières (AOC)") and has a Wednesday morning market.

[Lagrasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse "Lagrasse") stands on the [River Orbieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbieu "Orbieu") and has an 8th-century abbey, two bridges, and a well-preserved medieval stone village centre.

[Sigean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigean "Sigean"), 18 km south of [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), lies between the [A9 autoroute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A9_autoroute "A9 autoroute") and the coast and has an African [Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_reserve "Game reserve").

[Leucate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucate "Leucate") is a hilltop village, about 30 km south of Narbonne, which has spread down to the coast where Leucate Plage is a popular beach resort.

The [Corbières Massif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbi%C3%A8res_Massif "Corbières Massif") forms the central part of the department. It is an area of dissected plateaux and escarpments that form an effective barrier to direct road communication, characterized by steep hills, valleys, woodland, and vineyards. It contains several notable [Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar "Cathar") sites including [Quéribus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qu%C3%A9ribus "Quéribus"), [Peyrepertuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyrepertuse "Peyrepertuse"), and [Villerouge-Termenès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villerouge-Termen%C3%A8s "Villerouge-Termenès").

The [Lauragais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauragais "Lauragais"), that spreads on both sides of the administrative border between Aude and [Haute-Garonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute-Garonne "Haute-Garonne"), is a historic and cultural area known since the Middle Ages for its abundant agricultural productions. With [Castelnaudary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castelnaudary "Castelnaudary") as a central and major city, this region is also famous for the role it played during the [Albigensian Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade "Albigensian Crusade") and for its local heritage: Canal du Midi and its springs, abbeys and churches, castles, disk-shaped steles, dovecotes, windmills, bastides, etc.

Wine production is extensive across Aude, and local chateaux and domaines provide free tastings as well as sales of wine and other local produce. With the decline of some local wine production, local government policy is now to attract more tourists to the area, and to assist with this the Corbières area is now labelled on maps and road signs as [Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar "Cathar") country.

### Architectural heritage

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Architectural heritage")]

The Aude has about fifteen [bastides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastides "Bastides") which were built after the [Treaty of Meaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Meaux "Treaty of Meaux") in 1229 when the region was attached to the [Capetian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capetian_dynasty "Capetian dynasty") crown of France. The bastide is a type of town based on a grid created in one building project on a greenfield site. The purpose of such construction was to weaken the local lords and attract people to new economic centres. These bastides came into competition with fortified villages based on ecclesiastical or seigneurial power. [Chalabre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalabre "Chalabre"), [Camps-sur-l'Agly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camps-sur-l'Agly "Camps-sur-l'Agly") and the Bastide Saint-Louis in Carcassonne are examples of bastides in the Aude.

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg/250px-190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:190608_Burg-Puilaurens_01.jpg)

Puilaurens Castle

The department has many castles that have been developed by the General Council of the Aude to stimulate tourism. The fortresses are often located on rocky peaks, such as the castles of Quéribus and [Lastours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lastours "Lastours"), which gave them a strategic position. The city of Carcassonne was the logistical hub of the country at the time of conflict with the Kingdom of [Aragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aragon "Aragon").

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Fontfroide%2C_Arbeitshof.jpg/250px-Fontfroide%2C_Arbeitshof.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fontfroide,_Arbeitshof.jpg)

[Fontfroide Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontfroide_Abbey "Fontfroide Abbey"), Tourism highlight of Aude

Many abbeys exist throughout the department of Aude. The best known are [Fontfroide Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontfroide_Abbey "Fontfroide Abbey"), [Lagrasse Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrasse_Abbey "Lagrasse Abbey"), the abbey of Sainte-Marie [Villelongue-d'Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villelongue-d'Aude "Villelongue-d'Aude"), and the Abbey of [Saint-Hilaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Hilaire,_Aude "Saint-Hilaire, Aude").

[Narbonne Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne_Cathedral "Narbonne Cathedral") is a remarkable Gothic cathedral and remains unfinished. It is a symbol of the French presence in [Languedoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languedoc "Languedoc") in the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages").

### Caving

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Caving")]

Aude has many caves suitable for [speleological exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speleology "Speleology"). The _Pays de Sault_ consists of one of the largest limestone areas of the Pyrenees. This geology lends itself to the formation of cavities and there are many 'barrencs' (the local name for [Pit caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit_cave "Pit cave")). This plateau is home to a cave, the TM71, which is a superb cavity classified as a natural reserve since 1987. This is unique in France.

Other natural cavities of the Aude contain [concretions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concretions "Concretions") like the Pit cave of [Cabrespine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabrespine "Cabrespine"), the Aguzou Grotto, and the grotto of [Limousis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limousis "Limousis"). The latter contains the largest block of [aragonite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aragonite "Aragonite") yet discovered. In the Massif of Corbières on the plateau of Lacamp there are cavities formed by [detrital rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detritus_(geology) "Detritus (geology)") ([marls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marls "Marls"), [clays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay "Clay") and [puddingstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puddingstone_(rock) "Puddingstone (rock)")) carved by [erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erosion "Erosion").
