## Arts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Arts")]

### Cinema

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Cinema")]

The diversity of the landscape, its authenticity, and the uniqueness of its monuments have attracted many filmmakers. Thus, the city of [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne") has been the setting for many films. The excellent state of preservation of this city offers an outstanding setting for historical films. In 1908 filmmakers abandoned scenery on canvas and [Louis Feuillade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Feuillade "Louis Feuillade") filmed in front of the city towers for the _Return of the cross_, _Engagement oath_, and _Enchanted guitar_. In 1924 major films were produced such as _[Le Miracle des Loups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Miracle\_des\_loups\_(1924\_film) "Le Miracle des loups (1924 film)")_ by [Raymond Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Bernard_(filmmaker) "Raymond Bernard (filmmaker)"). In 1928 for the two thousandth anniversary of the city of Carcassonne, [Jean Renoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Renoir "Jean Renoir") made _Le Tournoi dans la cité_. In 1965 the city of Carcassonne appeared in _[The Sucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sucker "The Sucker")_ by [Gerard Oury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Oury "Gerard Oury"). In 1968 _[The Little Bather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Little\_Bather "The Little Bather")_ by [Robert Dhéry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Dh%C3%A9ry "Robert Dhéry") (with [Louis de Funès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_de_Fun%C3%A8s "Louis de Funès") and [Michel Galabru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Galabru "Michel Galabru")) shot at _Cabanes de Fleury_ (at the mouth of the Aude).

More recently, the Count's castle in the city was the setting for _[The Visitors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Visitors\_(1972\_film) "The Visitors (1972 film)")_ by [Jean-Marie Poire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Marie_Poire "Jean-Marie Poire") in 1972, while the [Château de Puivert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Puivert "Château de Puivert") was used in _La Passion Béatrice_ by [Bertrand Tavernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand_Tavernier "Bertrand Tavernier") in 1987, and _[The Ninth Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ninth\_Gate "The Ninth Gate")_ by [Roman Polanski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Polanski "Roman Polanski") in 1999. The Beach at [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") is present in [Betty Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Blue "Betty Blue") by [Jean-Jacques Beineix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Jacques_Beineix "Jean-Jacques Beineix").

### Painters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aude&action=edit&section=42 "Edit section: Painters")]

As for the cinema, it is the city of Carcassonne which attracts the greatest painters. [Jacques Ourtal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Ourtal?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jacques Ourtal (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques%20Ourtal "fr:Jacques Ourtal")] is the one who painted most of the city in trying to depict the city in different eras. Originally from [Fontiers-Cabardès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontiers-Cabard%C3%A8s "Fontiers-Cabardès"), the Aude painter _Eugène Pech_ has created paintings of the city many times which are today scattered in various public and private collections. The four eras of the city can still be found in settings for "The City Hall".

Another Aude artist, [Marie-Louise Petiet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Petiet "Marie Petiet"), is known for her transcriptions of scenes of popular life such as _La marchande d'oranges_ (The Orange Seller) or _La jeune fille aux oies_ (The young girl and the geese). Several of her works are visible at the Petiet Museum in Limoux. _Les blanchisseuses_ (The Laundresses) depicting a laundry lesson is particularly remarkable and well-known. Finally, [Paul Sibra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sibra "Paul Sibra"), an expert in landscape-painting, nicknamed "_le peintre du Lauragais_", produced thousands of paintings and drawings of scenes from or based on the rural life of the people of _Lauragais_ in the 1940s.

[Achille Laugé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille_Laug%C3%A9?action=edit&redlink=1 "Achille Laugé (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "fr:Achille Laugé"); [de](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "de:Achille Laugé"); [it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille%20Laug%C3%A9 "it:Achille Laugé")] (born 1861 in Arzens, died 1944 in Cailhau), misunderstood because of his pointillist technique, was able to show the dawning of spring especially with the [broom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broom_(shrub) "Broom (shrub)") and [almond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almond "Almond") trees in bloom.

Another artist, [Lina Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lina_Bill?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lina Bill (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lina%20Bill "fr:Lina Bill")] (real name Louis Bonnot), born at [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan "Gruissan") in 1855 and died in [Avignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon "Avignon") in 1936, painted Provence and the Mediterranean (museums of [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne "Narbonne"), [Carcassonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcassonne "Carcassonne"), and the [Musée d'Orsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mus%C3%A9e_d'Orsay "Musée d'Orsay") in Paris).
